title: Foreign investors withdrew from Malaysian equities for the fourth consecutive week, with net sales reaching MYR 885 million last week.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 3rd Report) Foreign funds have continued to flow out of Malaysian stocks for four consecutive weeks, with a net sell of MYR 884.6 million last week, significantly higher than the MYR 14.6 million recorded in the previous week.
According to the fund flow report by M&A Securities Research, foreign funds were net sellers of Malaysian equities over all five trading days last week, with Monday seeing the highest net selling at MYR 244 million.
This was followed by another MYR 237.2 million net sell on Tuesday. Although the pace of outflows slowed somewhat on Wednesday with a net sell of MYR 63.2 million, the exit accelerated again on Thursday and Friday, with net sales reaching MYR 124.3 million and MYR 216 million respectively.
In terms of specific sectors, the financial services sector saw the largest outflow of foreign funds (-MYR 513.7 million), followed by healthcare (-MYR 192.8 million) and utilities (-MYR 162.6 million).
As for sectors favored by foreign investors, these included plantations (MYR 151.2 million), technology (MYR 89.7 million), and communications and media (MYR 5.7 million).
On the other hand, local institutions continued to support the Malaysian stock market for the fourth consecutive week, with total net purchases amounting to MYR 812.7 million. Retail investors also ended seven consecutive weeks of net selling, purchasing MYR 72 million worth of shares last week.
In the first ten months of this year, foreign funds have net sold MYR 19.15 billion worth of Malaysian equities, while local institutions have consistently acted as stabilizers, net buying MYR 18.38 billion. Domestic retail investors contributed an additional MYR 770 million in net purchases.

author: Wai Keen103372792
body:
Can GENM Shareholders Still Sell Their Shares?
Yes, GENM shareholders can still sell their shares after the 75% threshold is reached.
Voluntary Decision: Accepting the offer at this stage is a voluntary decision for the remaining shareholders. The mandatory offer is in place to provide all shareholders an equal opportunity to exit the company at the offer price upon a change of control.
No Compulsory Acquisition (Yet): The offeror cannot compulsorily acquire the remaining shares until they have received acceptances of not less than 90% in value of the total offer shares (the shares they didn't already own).
Market Sale: Shareholders may also choose to sell their shares on the open market (Bursa Malaysia) if the offer remains open and the shares are still trading. However, once the 90% threshold is met, trading of shares may be suspended, and the stock could be delisted.
In summary, reaching 75% significantly increases the offeror's control and ability to pursue delisting, but individual shareholders retain the choice to sell their shares through the offer or on the market until the higher 90% compulsory acquisition threshold is triggered.

author: Wai Keen103372792
body:
Can GENM Shareholders Still Sell Their Shares?
Yes, GENM shareholders can still sell their shares after the 75% threshold is reached.
Voluntary Decision: Accepting the offer at this stage is a voluntary decision for the remaining shareholders. The mandatory offer is in place to provide all shareholders an equal opportunity to exit the company at the offer price upon a change of control.
No Compulsory Acquisition (Yet): The offeror cannot compulsorily acquire the remaining shares until they have received acceptances of not less than 90% in value of the total offer shares (the shares they didn't already own).
Market Sale: Shareholders may also choose to sell their shares on the open market (Bursa Malaysia) if the offer remains open and the shares are still trading. However, once the 90% threshold is met, trading of shares may be suspended, and the stock could be delisted.
In summary, reaching 75% significantly increases the offeror's control and ability to pursue delisting, but individual shareholders retain the choice to sell their shares through the offer or on the market until the higher 90% compulsory acquisition threshold is triggered.

body: Your question is highly pertinent. In fact—this is indeed one of the commonly used and most “sophisticated and discreet” strategies by many major shareholders during privatization processes. Let’s analyze in detail the possibility and rationale behind Lim Kok Thay’s “final-stage consolidation of allied votes” 👇 ⸻ 🧩 1. Theoretically: Entirely possible In the practical operations of mergers and acquisitions, this kind of **“deferred final consolidation”** does exist. The operational logic is as follows: 1. Initial stage: Strategic positioning and dispersed shareholding • If a major shareholder (e.g., Lim Kok Thay) has long intended to privatize the company, they will first discreetly purchase shares through trusted friends, family members, or long-term cooperative funds. • These 'allied' shares are temporarily not declared as 'acting in concert' because, on the surface, they appear to be independent investors. 2. Before the official announcement: Maintain distance to avoid triggering a Mandatory General Offer (MGO) • Malaysian regulations stipulate that once parties acting in concert collectively hold more than 33% of shares, a full takeover offer must be made. • Therefore, before the official announcement, these allies generally keep their total holdings below the 'safe threshold' of 32.99% to avoid regulatory triggers. 3. After the official announcement: Shares are 'recalled' during the public offer phase • Once Lim Kok Thay formally makes an acquisition offer (e.g., RM2.35), those allies can nominally 'accept the offer' and sell their shares to him. • From a market perspective, this is seen as 'ordinary shareholders responding to the acquisition'; from a strategic perspective, it is 'recalling votes within their own camp.' • This approach neither violates disclosure requirements nor safely and legally integrates 'private arrangements' under their name. 4. Final outcome • Before the official announcement: Control is concealed to avoid triggering regulatory scrutiny. • After the official announcement: Legal integration proceeds to achieve the target shareholding percentage. ⸻ ⚖️ II. The boundary between legality and gray areas The key to this approach lies in: • As long as the regulatory authority (SC Malaysia) cannot prove that these allies are 'acting in concert,' it remains a gray but compliant area. • However, if evidence (funding sources, shared directors, communication records) indicates that these individuals were instructed to purchase shares, violations may be retroactively enforced. In other words: ⚠️ 'Consolidating ally votes at the end' is a smart but high-risk strategy, As any revelation of behind-the-scenes coordination could lead to a violation of Rule 216 of the Takeover and Merger Code. ⸻ 📈 III. Practical Reference: Lim Kok Thay’s Personality and Past Actions Based on past cases (e.g., the 2019 acquisition of Genting Hong Kong assets or earlier equity adjustments at Genting Singapore), Lim Kok Thay's consistent strategy has been: • First, stabilize the situation (acquire shares up to a safety threshold) • Then, make an official announcement (triggering a rise in stock prices) • Finally, gradually integrate and slowly recoup investments This indicates that he is a highly disciplined capital operator who excels at leveraging timing differences and regulatory gaps. So, if asked, 'Will he wait until the last moment to acquire the remaining friendly shares?' My opinion is: ✅ Very likely. Moreover, it is highly probable that he has already planned the 'post-announcement share acquisition pathway.' ⸻ 🔍 IV. Three Signals You Can Observe If you want to verify whether he is truly 'collecting friendly votes at the final stage,' pay attention to the following in the coming weeks: 1. Changes in shareholding percentage • If he or Kien Huat rapidly increases their buying proportion in the open market over a short period (e.g., from 50% → 55% → 60%), it indicates that shares are quickly flowing back. 2. Trading volume characteristics • If there is a sudden surge in trading volume but the seller's identity remains undisclosed, it is highly likely that friendly accounts are 'cashing out.' 3. A surge in filings a few days before the offer period ends • Typically, as the offer approaches its deadline, a group of large shareholders will 'concentrate on accepting the offer,' which is often a pre-arranged setup.

body:
Decided to give up being a forward cannon in GENM and switch to following the main storyline.
1) This is an acquisition battle, not a merger battle. No major shareholder has come out in opposition. As a small retail investor, I am very clear whether I will be cannon fodder or part of the team.
2) Once 75% of shares are acquired and there are no more tradable shares in the market, it’s possible for trading to be suspended, potentially locking investors out for years. This isn’t investment; it’s suffering.
3) Regardless of how good future earnings might be, dividends are unlikely to ever be distributed to shareholders. Have you ever seen food supplies distributed to adversaries on the battlefield?
4) In previous acquisition battles, success was only possible if large funds or major shareholders stepped forward to challenge the outcome. Retail investors have always been minor players, merely along for the ride.

Here's the twist: foreign investors extended net selling to five weeks, dumping -RM85.4m. But local institutions bought for five weeks straight, injecting RM280.7m! author: Wai Keen103372792
body:
In Malaysia, companies seeking to delist after an MGO are required by law to provide an exit offer to minority shareholders. This is a general requirement under the Malaysian Code on Take-Overs and Mergers and Bursa Malaysia Listing Requirements to ensure minority shareholders are treated fairly and are not left holding unlisted shares that are difficult to sell. The requirement for a compulsory acquisition and subsequent delisting is typically triggered when the acquirer reaches or exceeds the 90% threshold of total shares.
However, the general legal framework in Malaysia ensures that:
For a voluntary delisting, approval from a 75% majority of shareholders is needed, and an exit offer must be made to all shareholders who object to the delisting.
For a mandatory general offer (MGO), if the acquirer's shareholding reaches 90% or more, they can compulsorily acquire the remaining shares, which effectively provides an exit for all remaining shareholders at the offer price.

However, the general legal framework in Malaysia ensures that:
For a voluntary delisting, approval from a 75% majority of shareholders is needed, and an exit offer must be made to all shareholders who object to the delisting.

For a mandatory general offer (MGO), if the acquirer's shareholding reaches 90% or more, they can compulsorily acquire the remaining shares, which effectively provides an exit for all remaining shareholders at the offer price.

title: Independent Advisor: Offer Unfair and Unreasonable; Recommend Rejection of Genting Malaysia Privatization
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 13th Report) Independent advisor Kenanga Investment Bank believes that the major shareholder, Genting,$GENTING (3182.MY)$ Offer to acquire all shares of Genting Malaysia at MYR 2.35 per share,$GENM (4715.MY)$ is "unfair and unreasonable," and recommends other shareholders reject the offer.
Kenanga Investment Bank’s independent research report released today highlights that the full acquisition price of MYR 2.35 per share, compared with Genting Malaysia's valuation using the Sum-of-the-Parts Valuation (SOPV) method, indicates a per-share value between MYR 3.48 and MYR 3.77, reflecting a discount of 32.47% to 37.67%.
At the same time, compared to the highest values over the past one year and two years, it reflects a relative discount of 3.69% to 19.52%; however, against the volume-weighted average price (VWAP) over more than two years, it shows a premium of 2.58%.
In view of this, Kenanga Investment Bank believes that the aforementioned acquisition is 'unfair.'
Active trading should not lead to delisting.
On the other hand, as the offeror, Genting also has no intention of maintaining the listing status of Genting Malaysia. However, given the active trading of Genting Malaysia over the past two months, it remains uncertain whether the offeror will be able to reach the 90% threshold required to apply for delisting. Therefore, Kenanga Investment Bank considers this acquisition 'unreasonable.'
The report mentioned that, as of November 6, the offeror held a total of 2.84033 billion shares in Genting Malaysia, equivalent to 50.11% of the latter's equity.
In other words, as long as Genting Malaysia continues to meet the public shareholding requirement and the offeror’s stake does not exceed 90%, its shares can continue to be traded on the main board.
It is worth noting that, as of September 2025, Genting Malaysia's average monthly trading volume over the past 24 months reached 193 million shares, accounting for 7.1% of the market's free float, reflecting active trading and liquidity even better than the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI's 6.48%.
After comprehensive consideration, Kenanga Investment Bank issued an 'unfair and unreasonable' recommendation and urged minority shareholders to reject the privatization proposal.
Independent directors maintain a unified position
Moreover, after evaluating the terms of the full acquisition and referencing Kenanga Investment Bank’s report, Genting Malaysia’s independent directors agreed that the offer is 'unfair' and 'unreasonable' to the company’s shareholders.
The independent directors pointed out that the full acquisition price does not adequately reflect the value of the company’s assets and its long-term growth potential, and lacks sufficient attractiveness to safeguard the best interests of minority shareholders.
Therefore, the independent directors unanimously recommended that shareholders reject the full acquisition offer and fully consider Genting Malaysia’s fundamentals and the potential for future business development before making a decision.
Converted into an unconditional full offer
As the full offer progresses, Genting has continued to increase its stake in Genting Malaysia at prices below the offer price of MYR 2.35 over the past five trading days. Its current shareholding has now exceeded 55%.
According to the announcement issued by Genting, as of November 13, the company had purchased a total of 34,929,300 shares, or 2.02% of Genting Malaysia's equity, through open market transactions at a full purchase price not exceeding MYR 2.35 per share.
To date, Genting holds 3,231,070,000 shares in Genting Malaysia, equivalent to 57.008% of its equity.
The deadline has been extended to December 1.
In view of this, Genting’s original conditional full takeover offer will become an unconditional full acquisition offer; meanwhile, the original deadline for the full acquisition will be extended from November 24 to 5:00 PM on December 1.
Spurred by the news of the full acquisition, Genting Malaysia’s trading volume in the market was highly active. Its stock price once rose to MYR 2.36, surpassing the full acquisition price of MYR 2.35 per share; however, it later retreated and closed flat at MYR 2.35, aligning with the privatization offer price.
As reported earlier, Genting plans to acquire all remaining shares of Genting Malaysia at MYR 2.35 per share, or up to MYR 6.7446 billion, and subsequently delist the latter through privatization.
Analysts have differing views
Genting’s plan to fully acquire and privatize Genting Malaysia has elicited different opinions among analysts.
Maybank Investment Banking analysts believe that the above offer did not take into account three major future benefits for Genting Malaysia, and the share price may rise as high as MYR 3.28. Genting needs to significantly increase its offer price to be fair, thus recommending shareholders to reject the offer.
Additionally, although TA Securities analysts agree that Genting’s full acquisition price is unattractive, they believe that it is unlikely that Genting will increase its offer.
The likelihood of Genting raising its offer is low, as the board of Genting Malaysia has no need to seek additional competitive acquisition proposals. Therefore, this offer may not receive sufficient support, and Genting Malaysia may ultimately fail to be privatized and delisted.
However, analysts at Galaxy International Securities hold a different view, suggesting that shareholders should accept the offer since Genting's bid is higher than their target price of MYR 1.88, providing shareholders with a decent exit opportunity.

title: Malaysia Morning Wrap | US government shutdown ends, but October inflation data lost and job report incomplete
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Key Takeaways:
• US Stock Market Tumbles as Tech and Non-Tech Sectors Face Broad Sell-Off
• US Government Shutdown Ends, but Economic Data Uncertainty Persists
• Bursa Malaysia Closes Marginally Higher After Choppy Trading Session
• Malaysian Market Sentiment Improves Amid Foreign Buying and Global Developments
• Stocks to watch: GENTING, PHARMA, etc.
🇺🇸Wall Street Summary
$S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ 6,737.49 (-1.66%)
$Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ 47,457.22 (-1.65%)
$Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ 22,870.36 (-2.29%)
Major US stock indexes experienced significant declines on Thursday, with the $Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ leading the downturn, falling 2.29% to 22,870.36. The $S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ dropped 1.66% to 6,737.49, while the $Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ fell 1.65% to 47,457.22.
The sell-off was broad-based, affecting both tech and non-tech sectors. Notable declines were seen in Big Tech companies like $Tesla (TSLA.US)$(-6.64%), $NVIDIA (NVDA.US)$(-3.58%), and $SanDisk Corp (SNDK.US)$(-16.96%), while non-tech Dow components such as $Goldman Sachs (GS.US)$ (-3.99%) and $Disney (DIS.US)$ (-7.75%) also suffered losses.
The 43-day U.S. government shutdown ended Wednesday night, with federal workers returning to their jobs on Thursday. However, the impact on economic data reporting remains significant. The White House announced that the October inflation report might never be released, and while the October nonfarm payrolls numbers will be published, the unemployment rate won't be compiled.
This data uncertainty has affected Federal Reserve decision-making, with Fed Chair Jerome Powell indicating it could influence the likelihood of a rate cut in December. The CME FedWatch tool now estimates the probability of a 25-point rate cut at the Fed's December meeting at 49.6%, down from 95.5% a month ago.
🇲🇾Bursa Market Insight
$FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ 1632.27 (+0.04%)
Top Gainer: $99SMART (5326.MY)$ RM3.200 (+1.91%)
Top Loser: $YTLPOWR (6742.MY)$RM3.790 (-2.57%)
USD/MYR: $USD/MYR (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.1290 (-0.17%)
The $FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ ended slightly higher on Thursday, gaining 0.66 points or 0.04% to close at 1,632.27, supported by banking and consumer stocks. The index experienced a volatile session, fluctuating between 1,631.15 and 1,635.27.
Despite the main index's positive close, losers outnumbered gainers 550 to 480. Market turnover improved to 3.95 billion units worth RM2.77 billion, reflecting increased trading activity compared to the previous day.

author: 大伯公
body: If the share price of Genting Malaysia Berhad (GENM) continues to trade above its privatization or takeover offer price, this typically suggests that the market assigns a higher valuation or holds positive expectations for the company, rather than simply accepting the offer price. Below are several possible interpretations and perspectives on this trend: 1. Market expectation that the offer price will be raised Basic perspective: Investors believe that the current offer price is too low to reflect the company's true intrinsic value or future potential. Market behavior: A share price trading above the offer price represents the market 'voting with their feet,' pressuring the bidding party to increase their offer. If the market believes there is a high likelihood of an increased offer, the share price will remain consistently above the offer price. 2. Potential existence of a 'competing bid' Basic perspective: Investors anticipate that another party or entity may propose a higher acquisition offer, commonly referred to as a 'white knight.' Market behavior: Such expectations can drive up the share price, as investors hope to sell their shares at a higher price to the competing bidder. 3. Market expectation that the takeover offer will fail Key Perspective: Investors may believe that this offer will ultimately fail to gain sufficient acceptance (e.g., not reaching the minimum required number of shares) or that regulatory authorities will not approve it. Market Behavior: If investors believe the offer will fail, they will evaluate the stock price based on the company's fundamentals and future outlook as an independent entity. If the company’s fundamentals are strong (e.g., improved performance, smooth progress in new projects), the stock price may reflect a higher valuation. 4. Positive changes in the company’s fundamentals Key Perspective: After the announcement of the offer, significant positive news may have emerged for the company (e.g., stronger-than-expected financial results, approval of a new business/casino, rapid recovery in tourism), which makes the value of the company operating independently already higher than the offer price. Market Behavior: The stock price reflects the latest fundamentals rather than the outdated offer price. 🤔 Conclusion and Key Observations This trend in stock price is a positive signal for shareholders. For existing shareholders: If you believe the offer price will increase or that a competitor may emerge, you can continue holding. If you think the company is more valuable without being acquired, you can also continue holding. For speculators: They may buy the stock, anticipating that the offer price will be raised (arbitrage opportunity). from ChatGPT.

title: Foreign funds net inflow to PMETAL RM237.1m as local institutions lean towards TENAGA
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
The 43-day U.S. government shutdown is finally over! This key development, coupled with shifting global economic data, set the stage for a mixed week in financial markets. While most global indices edged higher, money continued to flee from several Asian markets. However, Malaysia stood out with a notable reversal, attracting foreign cash after a five-week dry spell. Let's break down the flows.
Market Pulse
The week ended with a positive bias as 13 out of 20 tracked global indices closed higher. The end of the U.S. shutdown, alongside Trump's rollback of tariffs on over 200 food items, provided a boost. European markets led the charge, with France's CAC 40 up +2.8%. In contrast, Asian markets like the Philippines' PSEi (-3.0%) and Thailand's SET (-2.6%) were the worst performers. The FBM KLCI gained a modest +0.4%. The U.S. dollar weakened against the Ringgit by -1.1%, while Brent crude oil prices rose +1.2%.
Asia's Money Moves
Foreign investors extended a two-week net selling streak across Asia, pulling out a hefty -USD3.53 billion. The outflow was broad-based, with only India, Indonesia, and the Philippines seeing net inflows. India led with USD729.9m inflows, driven by plunging inflation that raised hopes for rate cuts. Indonesia extended its net buying streak to six weeks (USD229.9m), supported by a surge in consumer confidence. Meanwhile, South Korea saw outflows of -USD1.38b despite job gains, as labor market quality weakened.
Malaysia Breakdown
Malaysia's equity market witnessed a significant shift. Foreign investors ended a five-week selling spree, becoming net buyers with an inflow of RM476.1 million. They were net buyers on four out of five days. In contrast, local institutions turned net sellers (-RM318.1m), ending their five-week buying streak. Local retailers also extended their net selling to two weeks (-RM158.5m). The Average Daily Trading Volume (ADTV) saw a mixed picture: local institutions' activity rose +19.7%, while retailers and foreigners saw decreases of -5.0% and -2.5%, respectively.
Stock Spotlight: Who's Buying What?
Foreigners' Top Buys:
$PMETAL (8869.MY)$ (RM237.1m)
$GENM (4715.MY)$ (RM169.5m)
$MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ (RM161.2m)
Foreigners' Top Sells:
$KLK (2445.MY)$ (-RM73.7m)
$PBBANK (1295.MY)$ (-RM65.4m)
$TENAGA (5347.MY)$ (-RM63.6m)
Local Institutions' Top Buys:
$TENAGA (5347.MY)$ (RM87.9m)
$KLK (2445.MY)$ (RM74.6m)
$PBBANK (1295.MY)$ (RM74.0m)
Strategy Breakdown
– Foreigners' Logic: The return to Malaysia suggests a potential reassessment of regional risk or a search for value. Their top buys (Press Metal, banks) hint at a bet on commodity prices and domestic economic resilience.
– Local Institutions: Their selling after a long buying streak might indicate profit-taking. Their continued interest in heavyweights like $TENAGA (5347.MY)$ and $PBBANK (1295.MY)$ shows a defensive, value-oriented stance.
– Local Retailers: Their activity in stocks like $MMAG (0034.MY)$ points towards a focus on trading smaller caps and potential short-term momentum plays, contrasting with the larger players' strategies.
Risks to Watch
Investors should remain cautious. The U.S. funding bill only runs until January 2026, meaning political uncertainty could return swiftly. Globally, uneven economic growth—like the stagnation in major Euro-zone economies—poses a risk to the recovery narrative. For Malaysia, while domestic data is firm, the sustainability of foreign inflows will be key to watch amid global volatility.

title: Ending a five-week losing streak, foreign investors net purchased MYR 480 million worth of Malaysian stocks last week.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 17th) Foreign investors turned net buyers of Malaysian stocks last week with net purchases amounting to MYR 476.1 million, ending five consecutive weeks of net selling.
According to the capital flow report released by M&A Securities Investment Bank, foreign investors were net buyers on four out of the five trading days in the past week, including a significant net purchase of MYR 198.2 million worth of Malaysian shares last Tuesday.
Following that, they purchased MYR 193.9 million worth of Malaysian equities on Wednesday, and bought MYR 60.1 million and MYR 56.3 million worth of stocks on Monday and Thursday respectively.
However, after successive purchases, foreign investors turned to selling some shares on Friday, resulting in net sales of MYR 32 million.
In terms of sector distribution, consumer goods and services, financial services, and industrial products and services were the main sectors attracting net inflows from foreign investors last week, drawing in MYR 240 million, MYR 227.4 million, and MYR 181.4 million respectively.
On the other hand, local institutions turned into net sellers after five consecutive weeks of net inflows, selling stocks worth MYR 318.1 million.
Local retail investors, also net sellers, experienced an outflow of MYR 158.5 million.
Maybank Investment Bank noted that the average daily trading volume across the entire market declined last week. The average daily trading volume of local retail investors and foreign capital decreased by 5% and 2.5%, respectively, while institutional investor activity surged by 19.7%.
Top 10 net buy stocks by foreign capital: $PMETAL (8869.MY)$ , $GENM (4715.MY)$ , $MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ , $SDG (5285.MY)$ , $99SMART (5326.MY)$ , $CIMB (1023.MY)$ , $RHBBANK (1066.MY)$ , $FRONTKN (0128.MY)$ , $F&N (3689.MY)$ , $NESTLE (4707.MY)$

title: Foreign funds net outflow from PMETAL RM269.2M as local retail leans towards TENAGA
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
The global market faced mixed signals last week, with U.S. policy uncertainty and regional economic shifts driving cautious investor behavior. Here’s a breakdown of key developments and their implications.
1. Market Pulse
U.S. economic data presented a mixed picture: nonfarm payrolls rebounded strongly in September (+119k), but the Federal Reserve remains divided on the immediate need for interest rate cuts. Internationally, Eurozone inflation held steady at 2.1%, while the UK saw a moderation. China maintained its benchmark lending rates, reflecting a wait-and-see approach despite soft economic indicators. Consequently, 16 of 20 major global indices declined, with the Philippines' PSEI (+7.4%) and Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh VSE (+1.2%) being notable exceptions. Commodity markets saw Brent crude oil fall 2.84% to USD62.56 per barrel. The prevailing mood was one of caution as investors awaited clearer policy direction.
2. Asia’s Money Moves
Foreign investors were net sellers across the eight Asian markets tracked, with total outflows reaching USD6.73 billion, nearly double the previous week's amount. The flow distribution was uneven:
Net Inflows: India (USD261.3m) and Indonesia (USD233.5m) attracted foreign capital, supported by domestic factors. The Philippines also saw modest inflows (USD51.4m).
Net Outflows: South Korea experienced significant outflows (-USD2.30b), and Thailand extended its outflow streak to four weeks (-USD108.5m).
The drivers were equally varied, ranging from domestic policy stability in inflow countries to growth concerns and geopolitical uncertainties in others.
3. Malaysia Breakdown
Foreign investors reversed to net sellers, offloading RM1.03 billion after a brief buying spell. Outflows peaked on Tuesday (-RM458.5m). Local institutions capitalized, becoming net buyers (RM1.01 billion), while retailers added RM28.1 million. Trading volume rose for foreigners (+16.8%) and institutions (+2.3%), but retail activity dipped slightly (-0.3%).
4. Stock Spotlight: Who’s Buying What?
Local Retailers favored stability:
Top Buys: $TENAGA (5347.MY)$ (RM26.4m)
Top Sells: $GENM (4715.MY)$ (-RM60.4m)
Institutions leaned into commodities and healthcare:
Top Buys: $PMETAL (8869.MY)$ (RM276.5m)
Top Sells: $SDG (5285.MY)$ (-RM137.1m)
Foreigners dumped industrials for plantations:
Top Buys: $SDG (5285.MY)$ (RM133.2m)
Top Sells: $PMETAL (8869.MY)$ (-RM269.2m)
5. Strategy Breakdown: A Clash of Perspectives?
The divergent flows highlight different investor priorities. Local Institutions appeared to take a contrarian, value-oriented approach, stepping in to buy during foreign selling, particularly in large-cap names. Local Retailers engaged in more selective, sentiment-driven trading. Foreign Investors prioritized global risk management, reducing exposure to certain industrial and utility sectors while showing preference for defensive plays like plantations. This contrast underscores a difference in time horizon and risk appetite between local and international players.
6. Risks to Watch
Key near-term risks include continued U.S. policy uncertainty, as a divided Fed could prolong market volatility. Slowing global growth prospects, evidenced by softer data from China and Thailand, may weigh on export-oriented economies. Additionally, fluctuations in key commodity prices like oil and palm oil remain a critical factor for regional markets.

The $富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ fell 7.04 points, or 0.43% to 1,617.46. Bursa Malaysia declined on Thursday, dragged by PETRONAS-linked stocks and a cautious market mood.
Dealers noted that traders are maintaining a selective stance and expect the ongoing flow of corporate earnings to keep offering short-term opportunities.
Malaysia's producer price index (PPI) declined 0.1% year-on-year in October, improving from the 0.8% drop recorded in September, according to data released Thursday by the Department of Statistics Malaysia.
Despite ongoing global uncertainties, Malaysia’s economy is still projected to grow in 2026, though at a more moderate pace, as key indicators show no signs of an imminent recession, economists say. Most economists forecast that Malaysia's economy will grow by 4.3% to 4.7% year-on-year in 2026. The economic growth rate for the first nine months of 2025 stood at 4.7%.
🔍IPO Scanner
🔔Stocks to Watch
$INARI (0166.MY)$ saw its first-quarter net profit surge 113.5% year-on-year to RM51.5 million, up from RM24.1 million, largely driven by favourable foreign-exchange moves. Revenue for Q1 2026 slid 16% to RM325.8 million from RM388 million, as weaker demand and reduced customer orders cut loading volumes across all segments.
$YTL (4677.MY)$ posted a 3.8% rise in net profit to RM346.48 million for Q1 2026, up from RM333.71 million a year ago, even as revenue dipped 1.7% to RM7.64 billion from RM7.77 billion.
$YTLPOWR (6742.MY)$—majority-owned by YTL Corp with a 52.46% stake—lifted first-quarter net profit 6.4% to RM500.57 million from RM470.6 million a year earlier, even as revenue eased 5.7% to RM5.36 billion from RM5.68 billion.
$HLBANK (5819.MY)$’s net profit remained flat at RM1.09 billion, or 53.2 sen per share, as increased impairment losses and weaker associate income outweighed lower operating expenses.
$RHBBANK (1066.MY)$ posted a record quarterly net profit of RM904 million for Q3 2025, up 8.5% year-on-year, lifted by stronger non-interest income and a sharp drop in credit-loss provisions. Year-on-year, net interest income grew 0.8% while non-interest income expanded 4.6%.
$SIME (4197.MY)$ reported on Thursday that first-quarter net profit fell 56% year-on-year to RM355 million, as the prior-year figure had been lifted by a one-off gain from a land sale. Revenue for Q3 2025 eased to RM18.03 billion from RM18.26 billion.
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ reported an 86.5% plunge in Q3 2025 net profit to RM30.3 million (from RM223.8 million last year), hit by smaller forex gains, lower interest income and higher depreciation, even as revenue rose 14.25% to RM7.48 billion.
$GENM (4715.MY)$ saw its third-quarter net profit plunge 79% year-on-year, dragged down by a steep drop in unrealised foreign-exchange gains. Profit for Q3 2025 came in at RM119.7 million versus RM569.2 million a year ago, after forex-related income collapsed to RM2.8 million from RM601.8 million. Top-line momentum stayed strong, however, with revenue rising 22% to RM3.36 billion from RM2.75 billion.
$AXIATA (6888.MY)$ swung to a RM27.35 million net loss in the third quarter after it took a heavy impairment on the value of its assets. Revenue at Malaysia’s largest telecom operator by sales eased roughly 5% year-on-year to RM2.92 billion for the three months ended 30 September 2025.
$MALAKOF (5264.MY)$ reported a 67.5% drop in net profit to RM28.21 million for Q3 2025, down from RM86.88 million a year ago, as a steam-turbine pipe leak at the Tanjung Bin Energy plant cut energy payments.
$BJCORP (3395.MY)$ logged a sixth-consecutive quarterly loss after tax charges wiped out operating profit. The net deficit for Q1 2026 narrowed sharply to RM10.94 million from RM167.85 million a year earlier, helped by smaller foreign-exchange losses, according to a stock-exchange filing. Quarterly revenue advanced 3.6 % year-on-year to RM2.31 billion.

title: New York casino license and privatization deadlines coincide; could Genting Malaysia's acquisition price increase?
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 28th) Genting Malaysia $GENM (4715.MY)$ recently delivered a weak earnings performance, drawing market attention to the announcement of the New York casino license results on December 1. Some reiterated that Genting's $GENTING (3182.MY)$ privatization offer price of MYR 2.35 does not reflect the potential value associated with the New York casino license.
Maybank Investment Bank analysts noted in their earnings report that due to seasonally higher expenses at Resorts World Genting (RWG), coupled with reduced winter visitors to its West Coast US operations, Genting Malaysia’s EBITDA for the fourth quarter is expected to weaken on a quarter-on-quarter basis.
However, he also stated that the market is now focused on the outcome of Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) casino license in New York's downstate commercial casino bidding and estimates that expansion-related profits will peak in 2030 at approximately MYR 1.93 billion.
The analyst reiterated his recommendation that shareholders reject the mandatory general offer (MGO) at MYR 2.35 per share, expressing confidence that Genting Malaysia will secure the casino license, a value not reflected in the MYR 2.35 acquisition price.
Genting's stake increases to 63.38%
On another note, Public Investment Bank analysts mentioned that Genting has extended the deadline for its voluntary offer from November 24 to December 1, coinciding with the day the New York State Gaming Commission (NYSGC) will announce the results of the casino license bidding.
“If Genting fails to achieve sufficient acceptance rates, it may need to raise its offer price, especially if Genting Malaysia successfully secures the casino license.”
The analyst also added that Genting Malaysia’s independent advisor has recommended shareholders to reject the MYR 2.35 offer, deeming it “unfair” and “unreasonable.”
According to the Bursa Malaysia announcement, Genting's shareholding in Genting Malaysia as of yesterday was 63.38%.
CIMB Investment Bank analysts also noted that Resorts World New York's Q3 EBITDA fell by 13% year-on-year due to the casino clearing some gaming spaces to install new gaming tables and slot machines after securing the casino license.
Core earnings forecasts significantly upgraded
“Resorts World Genting’s Q3 revenue increased by 22% year-on-year, with EBITDA margins expanding by 2.1 percentage points. We have raised our core EPS forecasts for fiscal years 2025 to 2027 by 58% to 69% to reflect these positive developments.”
Maybank Investment Bank maintained its 'Buy' rating on Genting Malaysia, raising the target price from MYR 2.91 to MYR 3.27; Public Investment Bank reiterated its 'Short-term Buy' rating, increasing the target price from MYR 1.84 to MYR 2.35; CIMB Investment Bank maintained its 'Hold' rating, revising the target price upwards from MYR 2.35 to MYR 2.55.
However, Maybank Investment Bank and CIMB Investment Bank also indicated that if Genting Malaysia wins the New York casino license, their respective target prices could increase by 47 sen and 52 sen.
Source: Nanyang Business Daily

author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Global markets navigated softening US indicators and shifting central bank policies, while Asia faced another week of foreign capital flight. Here's how money moved across markets and what it means for investors.
Market Pulse
US economic signals softened as the government shutdown's impact lingered. Retail growth slowed to +0.2% in September, while consumer confidence dipped. The Fed held rates steady, but the Bank of Korea turned hawkish, shaking investor sentiment. Most global indices rose – Nasdaq led with a +4.91% weekly gain – but Malaysia's FBM KLCI fell -0.81%. Brent crude climbed +1.02% to USD63.20/barrel, and the Ringgit strengthened slightly against the USD.
Asia's Money Moves
Foreign investors remained net sellers across eight Asian markets for the week ended 28 November 2025, with total outflows reaching USD1.17 billion-though this was about 5.8 times lower than the previous week. Indonesia led with net inflows of USD59.5 million, marking its eighth consecutive week of foreign buying, while India recorded modest inflows of USD1.1 million. South Korea saw the largest outflows at USD1.0 billion, followed by Thailand and the Philippines.
Key drivers included cautious investor sentiment after the Bank of Korea signaled a pause in its easing cycle, Indonesia's relative stability despite severe flooding in Sumatra, and India's stronger-than-expected GDP growth of +8.2% in the third quarter. Regional trade imbalances and currency volatility also influenced fund movements.
Malaysia Breakdown
Foreign investors extended net selling in Malaysia to two consecutive weeks, with outflows of -RM484.8m. Local institutions continued buying (RM356.4m net), and local retailers also turned net buyers (RM128.4m). Average daily trading volume rose across the board, with foreign participation surging +42%.
Stock Spotlight: Who's Buying What?
Foreign Investors favored $TM(4863.MY)$ (RM170.7m), $MAYBANK(1155.MY)$ (RM106.8m), and $GENM(4715.MY)$ (RM65.8m).
Local Institutions piled into $TENAGA(5347.MY)$ (RM292.7m), $SUNWAY(5211.MY)$ (RM151.1m), and $PMETAL(8869.MY)$ (RM101.8m).
Local Retailers bought $IOICORP(1961.MY)$ (RM60.5m), $YTLPOWR(6742.MY)$ (RM52.4m), and $CHINHIN(5273.MY)$ (RM52.1m).
Strategy Breakdown: Who's Betting on What?
Local institutions are leaning into utilities and financials – a defensive, policy-aligned play. Retail investors are chasing construction and consumer stocks, suggesting short-term momentum trading. Foreigners are selling energy and industrial goods, likely hedging against global uncertainty and Ringgit volatility.
Risks to Watch
Keep an eye on US inflation trends, Asian central bank policy shifts, and commodity price swings – especially oil and palm oil, which impact Malaysia's export outlook.

title: Genting Malaysia's privatization falls short, brokers anticipate a second wave of actions
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
Genting Malaysia Privatization Falls Short of Requirements Securities firms anticipate a second wave of actions. Reported by Lin Disheng Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$ full acquisition and privatization of Genting Malaysia $GENM (4715.MY)$ The offer, which concluded at 5 p.m. today, resulted in Genting raising its stake to 73.133%, but it failed to meet the 90% threshold required for completing the privatization. Market observers believe that Genting may subsequently raise its bid and continue pursuing the privatization of Genting Malaysia. According to the announcement, as of 5 p.m. today, Genting holds a total of 4.144 billion shares or 73.133% of Genting Malaysia's equity, an increase from 2.833 billion shares or 49.999% when the full acquisition offer was made, representing an additional 1.311 billion shares or 23.134%. Nevertheless, the above-mentioned shareholding ratio not only falls short of the 90% mandatory general offer threshold but also remains below 75%, indicating that the public float is still above the minimum regulatory requirement of 25% for listing. Huang Zhuhao, Founder and CEO of Tradeview Capital, pointed out in a telephone interview with Nanyang Siang Pau that although this privatization attempt has fallen through, Genting is likely to raise its offer further to push forward with the privatization of Genting Malaysia. “Considering that Genting has made significant efforts for the privatization plan, even resorting to debt financing to secure the acquisition funds, I believe that Genting is determined to privatize Genting Malaysia, and therefore, it is very likely to further increase its offer going forward.” An increase in the offer price to MYR 2.80 is anticipated. He predicted that Genting may subsequently raise its bid to between MYR 2.50 and MYR 2.80. Previously, Genting announced a bid of MYR 2.35 per share, or a total of MYR 6.7 billion, for a full takeover of Genting Malaysia. Ng Huang Han also noted that if Genting merely intended to increase its stake in Genting Malaysia to strengthen control, there would be no need to go through the trouble of pursuing a privatization plan. He believed that Genting’s decision to privatize might be based on two considerations. “Genting may feel that Genting Malaysia’s value has been significantly undervalued, and there is no need for both companies to be listed simultaneously. Moreover, after privatization, Genting Malaysia will have greater flexibility to expand in the U.S. market without being constrained by Bursa Malaysia.” Huang Han also pointed out that the outcome of the bidding process for casino licenses in New York's lower state will further clarify the prospects for Genting Malaysia. The local government of New York will announce the results of the bidding process for the casino licenses on December 1, local time. As Genting Malaysia is one of the three remaining bidders, and the New York State government may issue three licenses, the market believes that the company is almost certain to win.

title: GENT has successfully acquired 73.133% of GENM's shares, with the acquisition period officially closing at 5 PM on December 1, 2025. The next step is to see
author: 心如紫水
body: GENT has successfully acquired 73.133% of GENM's shares, with the acquisition period officially closing at 5 PM on December 1, 2025. The next step is to see how it performs in taking the company private with a 90% stake… Perhaps it could be made into a TV series in n years… 🤔 So the acquisition period has officially closed. Are you planning to sell GENM to Genting now? It’s too late; there’s no RM2.35 offer anymore. So, does that mean trading can only happen at market price? The entire process has now entered the second phase. Or 🤔 will Genting offer a better price to acquire more shares? The parent company originally held 49.999%, and during this acquisition period, an additional 20.887% was sold to them by shareholders, plus 2.247% acquired through other agreements, bringing their total ownership to 73.133%. This means that Resorts World Genting has regained control of 73% of the company. Uncle Lim has taken back his chips from the casino. So … there is enough material to discuss over coffee this entire week. To privatize a publicly listed company, there are two approaches: ① Voluntary Offer ② Mandatory Take-Over Offer The first phase has now been completed. However, privatization has not yet occurred as the threshold of 90% has not been reached. The #Compulsory Acquisition for delisting is only triggered upon reaching 90%. Currently, only 73% has been acquired, leaving a shortfall of 17%. But if you ask me, 'Is the direction clear?' I will only say this: If Genting merely intended to increase its stake slightly, it wouldn't have gone as far as 73%. Those who aim big don’t stop halfway. If they are going to do it, they will see it through to the end. They’ve come this far already… Since they’re here…

author: 心如紫水
body:
Finally, GenM has successfully secured its gaming license in New York! Could this be Tan Sri’s ultimate plan behind insisting on privatizing GenM? The GenM Resorts World project represents the largest investment among the three casino proposals, amounting to USD 5.5 billion. It also has the potential to become one of the largest casinos in New York. On the other hand, it was initially believed that achieving a 75% ownership stake for Genting's privatization would be a distant goal. However, within less than two months, Tan Sri directly increased his stake to 73%, leaving only a 2% gap to reach the 75% threshold for delisting. An additional investment of MYR 200-300 million could complete the privatization process. But anyhow, the RM2.35 offer officially closed at 5 PM yesterday. This means that from today onward, Genting’s stock price may experience significant volatility. If I recall correctly, GenM should still have the option to extend its offer until January next year. However, it remains uncertain whether Tan Sri will exercise this option. In the event that GenM does proceed with the delisting, shareholders will need to manage their own positions independently. Nevertheless, there have been previous examples of privatizations: due to the reduced presence of retail investors and the remaining stakeholders being closely aligned, companies often distribute exceptionally high dividends to shareholders. Based on Tan Sri’s track record over the years, do you think he leans more towards being generous or frugal?

body:
📌 [Article 2 | Why 75% ≠ Delisting?]

Many friends have recently asked:
"Is it possible to delist once exceeding 75%?"
"Is 75% the threshold for privatization?"

❌ Not at all.
In Malaysia, 75% is not a condition for delisting.

⭐ ① The 75% figure represents Bursa’s 'Public Spread' requirement (not a delisting threshold).

The rule is straightforward:

Listed companies must maintain ≥ 25% of shares held by the public (public spread).
Therefore, major shareholders can hold a maximum of 75%.

What happens if it exceeds 75%?

❌ It will not be automatically delisted.
❌ Mandatory acquisition is not allowed.
✔ It only triggers Bursa’s regulatory oversight (to restore public spread).

📌 Have you seen someone say, 'Exceeding 75% will lead to delisting'?
That is a misunderstanding.

⭐ So why do people keep talking about 75%?

Because 75% appears in another mechanism:

🟦 Voluntary Delisting

According to Bursa’s rules:
✔ At least 75% of shareholders vote in favor,
✔ The number of opposing votes is less than 10%,
✔ An exit offer must be provided,
If the above conditions are met, the company can apply for voluntary delisting.

However, note the following:

❗ Voluntary delisting ≠ Mandatory privatization
❗ Minority shareholders cannot be forcibly bought out,
❗ It is an entirely different process

⭐ ③ The only threshold that truly determines "mandatory privatization" is:
⭐ ≥ 90% (Take-over Code + CMSA Section 222)

Reaching 90%:
✔ The acquirer can initiate a Compulsory Acquisition.
✔ Minority shareholders are required to sell their shares.
✔ The company can officially go private and be delisted.

Below 90%:
❌ GENM cannot be forcibly privatized.
❌ The acquisition process is not considered complete.
❌ The company remains listed.
✔ Minority shareholders retain the option to decide whether or not to sell.

⭐ Final summary in one sentence.
75% = Voluntary delisting voting threshold (requires opposition votes <10%)
90% = True threshold for mandatory privatization & compulsory acquisition

author: J00Y
body:
I think so.
First: The New York casino will consume a significant amount of capital.

Second: At the time, some institutions, funds, or even retail investors may have purchased shares at $2.36 to compete with Mr. Lin for the shares, betting that he would extend the offer period and increase the bid price to acquire those shares. However, once the offer period ended, the anticipated scenario did not materialize—Mr. Lin neither raised the acquisition price nor extended the offer period.

Third: The tender offer has expired, and buying interest has disappeared. Who will provide support? Retail investors?Therefore, without continued strong buying support, prices are likely to fall due to an oversupply situation.

Fourth: Mr. Lin already holds 73.13% of the shares. According to regulations, after the expiration of the tender offer, Mr. Lin can continue to acquire up to an additional 2% of the target company's shares within one year. This would bring his ownership to exactly 75%, meeting the threshold to apply for delisting. If less than 10% of shareholders oppose the delisting at the shareholder meeting, the delisting will be successful. Remaining shareholders who did not sell will become private shareholders of the company, and their shares will no longer be tradable on the open market—they would need to find buyers privately. Even if more than 10% of shareholders oppose the delisting, it is not problematic because Mr. Lin already controls the company and can make many decisions. He can afford to wait patiently until dissenting shareholders capitulate.

Fifth: Given the substantial capital requirements of the New York casino project, it is highly unlikely that the company will pay dividends even if shares are held long-term. Some shareholders may choose to sell rather than endure a prolonged holding period, seeking better opportunities in other stocks.

title: Malaysia Morning Wrap | Genting Malaysia Secures New York Casino License
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Key Takeaways:
• Crypto Rally Fuels U.S. Major Indices Gains on Tuesday
• Bursa Malaysia Extends Winning Streak to Two Days
• Risks Persist Going into 2026 After Malaysia’s Strong Manufacturing PMI Recovery
• Stocks to watch: Genting Malaysia, YTL Power, etc.
🇺🇸Wall Street Summary
$标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ 6,829.37 (+0.25%)
$道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ 47,474.46 (+0.39%)
$纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ 23,413.67 (+0.59%)
On Tuesday, U.S. major indices all climbed, lifted by a bounce in crypto, a strong showing from index heavyweight Boeing, and post-earnings rallies in tech leaders MongoDB and Credo.
The $纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ added 137.75 points (0.6%) to a 23,413.67 close, while the $道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ rose 185.13 ticks (0.4%) to 47,474.46 and the $标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ gained 16.74 points (0.3%) to 6,829.37.
$Bitcoin (BTC.CC)$ led the rebound, climbing 6.7% to $91,143.22 by late afternoon in New York. Other digital currencies also posted substantial gains, with $Solana (SOL.CC)$ jumping 11.6% to $138.98, $Ethereum (ETH.CC)$ rising 8.6% to $2,990.49, and $Ripple (XRP.CC)$ increasing 7.3% to $2.16.
$波音 (BA.US)$ surged 10.2% after its CFO pledged the planemaker will swing to positive free cash flow in 2026—its first time since 2023. The Dow and S&P heavyweight also landed a $104.4 million Navy contract to overhaul military-aircraft displays.
Elsewhere, tech names $MongoDB (MDB.US)$ and $Credo Technology (CRDO.US)$ took off: MongoDB jumped 22.2% on strong guidance, while Credo closed 10.1% higher after touching an intraday record on well-received quarterly results.
The National Retail Federation announced on Tuesday that a record-breaking 202.9 million Americans shopped during the five-day stretch from Thanksgiving to Cyber Monday, the traditional kickoff to the U.S. holiday season.
President Donald Trump revealed he will name his pick to succeed Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell early next year. Powell’s term expires in May, and the two have frequently been at odds.
🇲🇾Bursa Market Insight
$富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ 1630.6 (+0.37%)
Top Gainer: $NESTLE (4707.MY)$ RM120.2 (+7.71%)
Top Loser: $PPB (4065.MY)$ RM10.1 (-4.54%)
USD/MYR: $美元/马来西亚令吉 (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.1325 (+0.04%)
The $富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ closed up 6.03 points, or 0.37%, at 1,630.60. Bursa Malaysia closed higher on Tuesday, as the FBM KLCI gained ground despite persistent selling across the wider market.
Analysts caution that Malaysia’s manufacturing rebound may struggle to carry its current momentum into 2026.
According to TA Securities, next year’s expansion hinges on how well the sector handles a confluence of risks: weakening U.S. orders, escalating geopolitical frictions, fresh supply-chain shocks, rising input costs, a stronger ringgit that erodes export price competitiveness, and possible delays in capital-investment timelines.
🔍IPO Scanner
🔔Stocks to Watch
$GENM (4715.MY)$ has secured one of the three highly sought-after casino licenses in New York. The company’s subsidiary, Genting New York LLC, has been selected by the New York Gaming Facility Location Board to proceed to the final stage of licensing review by the New York State Gaming Commission. The board is expected to finalize and announce the license awards by December 31, 2025.
$CDB (6947.MY)$, $MAXIS (6012.MY)$, and $YTLPOWR (6742.MY)$ will each pay RM327.9 million to buy the government’s stake in Digital Nasional Bhd.
$COASTAL (5071.MY)$ intends to sell two ships for a total of RM187.6 million.
$AWC (7579.MY)$’s wholly owned subsidiary, Trackwork & Supplies Sdn Bhd, has secured a contract worth nearly RM59 million from Prasarana Malaysia Bhd to replace aluminum power conductor rails on the Ampang Line.
$DELEUM (5132.MY)$’s subsidiary, Turboservices Sdn Bhd (90% indirectly owned), has secured a six-year contract to service solar turbine turbomachinery for PETRONAS Carigali, the exploration arm of Petroliam Nasional Bhd (PETRONAS).

title: RCE Capital: Turnaround Signal, Returning to Growth Trajectory! A Positive Shift! The price has just broken above the MA200, signaling bullish uptrend!
author: TenBagger Research
body:
RCE Capital’s latest quarterly results have delivered a highly positive signal: the company has ended a streak of seven consecutive quarters of year-on-year earnings decline and is officially back on a growth path.
Over previous quarters, RCE's profitability was under pressure due to increased impairment allowances resulting from a higher attrition rate among civil servants. The rebound in profit this quarter suggests that the worst of these headwinds may now be behind the company.
Dividend & Yield Outlook : Dividend Declared: First interim dividend of 3.0 sen. Ex-Date: December 16, 2025. Yield Estimation: Assuming a full-year payout of 6.0 – 10.0 sen (historically paid in two tranches, occasionally with special dividends) and based on the current share price of approximately RM 1.2 the estimated dividend yield is between 5% – 6%.
Key Catalyst: Civil Service Salary Hike Upcoming Adjustment: The Malaysian government has announced a salary increment for civil servants. Timeline: Expected to take formal effect in January 2026 (partial adjustment). Impact: As RCE Capital’s core business revolves around civil servant financing, this salary hike is expected to improve borrower credit quality and loan eligibility, serving as a significant tailwind for the company moving forward.
Take note :the price has just broken above the MA200, signaling a trend reversal to bullish. This is the first time this year, and it’s a strong bullish indicator.
Major Shareholder Action: A Strong Vote of Confidence Tan Sri Azman Bin Hashim’s Accumulation The continuous buying by Tan Sri Azman Bin Hashim (via his investment vehicle, Cempaka Empayar Sdn Bhd) is a significant market signal. His stake is now approaching the 60% threshold, indicating a high level of conviction in the company’s prospects.

title: It’s not that we aren’t smart; it’s just that at every turning point, we’re always half a step behind. By the time we see the news, prices have already surged;
author: 心如紫水
body:
It’s not that we aren’t smart; it’s just that at every turning point, we’re always half a step behind. By the time we see the news, prices have already surged; by the time we read the announcements, others are already in the second round of the game. This Genting acquisition of GENM is an acquisition for them, but for us retail investors, it feels more like a harvest.

For major investors, it’s 'I think it’s undervalued, so I’ll buy and hold.'
For retail investors, it’s 'I think it’s undervalued, but the price keeps dropping as I buy.'

Genting is having a great time with this acquisition, but what about retail investors? What are we acquiring? Notices, lessons, and a bunch of question marks. Otherwise… do you really think you’re getting mooncakes for the Mid-Autumn Festival?

but anywhere … has this wave of experience points increased?

title: Where Are Malaysia's Earnings Growth Engines Amid Sector Divergence?
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
As Malaysia’s latest reporting season draws to a close, investors are increasingly focused on which sectors managed to deliver earnings outperformance and emerge as the market’s “growth engines”, and which ones have buckled under high bases and cyclical headwinds.
Overall, brokers broadly characterise corporate results as resilient, but with widening dispersion and more pronounced sector rotation.
According to Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB), about 24% of its coverage universe beat expectations, with the earnings “beat-to-miss” ratio improving from 0.77 times to 0.84 times, indicating a modest uptick in positive surprises. CIMB Securities’ latest review shows a similar pattern: roughly 21% of covered companies reported earnings above expectations, while 27% came in below, with the beat-to-miss ratio improving to around 1.8 times, underscoring that overall earnings momentum remains intact despite pockets of weakness.
Moomoo news team highlights several key sectors that investors should watch closely:
Growth Engines: Three Core Pillars and Consumer Outperformers
Amid a broadly challenging macro environment, a number of cash-generative or cyclically supported sectors have emerged as the main pillars of earnings growth this quarter, delivering both solid results and supportive share-price reactions.
Banking: Stable Earnings and Valuation Catch-Up
Within financials, major lenders including $MAYBANK (1155.MY)$, $AMBANK (1015.MY)$, $RHBBANK (1066.MY)$ and $AFFIN (5185.MY)$ maintained a broadly steady performance over the quarter. Supported by healthy loan growth and stable-to-marginally-compressed net interest margins (NIMs), alongside well-contained non-performing loan (NPL) ratios, most banks recorded year-on-year growth in core net profit. Several names even modestly beat consensus expectations, creating room for further valuation normalisation and sustaining interest from both domestic and foreign funds.
Read more: Malaysian Banking Stocks Hit Record Highs on Solid Fundamentals
Plantations: Higher CPO Prices Drive Earnings Rebound
The plantation sector saw a meaningful earnings recovery on the back of relatively elevated crude palm oil (CPO) prices. Estimates suggest that, with average CPO prices trending higher year-on-year and unit production costs remaining well managed, sector quarterly earnings rose by more than 40% on a year-on-year basis. Sector bellwethers such as $SDG (5285.MY)$, $KLK (2445.MY)$, $TAANN (5012.MY)$ and $GENP (2291.MY)$ generally delivered results that exceeded market expectations, supported by recovering yields and disciplined cost control, reinforcing confidence in the sector’s medium-term prospects.
Building Materials and Construction Value Chain: Project Execution Unlocks Earnings Leverage
Building materials and construction-related counters posted a notably strong quarter. Sell-side estimates indicate that sector earnings improved by close to 70% year-on-year, highlighting significant operating leverage at play. Aluminium and materials producers (such as $PMETAL (8869.MY)$) reported substantial profit recovery, driven by higher volumes, better plant utilisation, and more stable pricing. At the same time, leading contractors like $GAMUDA (5398.MY)$ benefited from robust order books and steady progress on both domestic and overseas projects, confirming earnings resilience and enhancing visibility on medium-term workloads.
Retail and Services: Value-for-Money “Counter-Cyclical” Growth
Amid growing consumption stratification and more value-conscious spending, retailers and service providers focused on essential, value-for-money offerings have managed to grow against the cycle through store expansion and lean operations. Leading convenience chain $99SMART (5326.MY)$ and mass-market coffee brand $KOPI (0338.MY)$, for example, have leveraged their affordable positioning to capture the trading-down trend, supporting strong growth and notable share-price outperformance this earnings season.
Read more: KOPI Maintains Growth Momentum. What Do You Need to Know?
Sectors Under Pressure: Impairments and Margin Squeeze in Non-financial Heavyweights
In stark contrast to the above growth segments, several non-financial heavyweights have reported weaker earnings or one-off impairments this quarter, prompting meaningful share-price corrections and weighing on the benchmark in the near term.
Utilities and Cyclical Chemicals: Impairments Magnify Earnings Volatility
Within utilities and energy-linked chemicals, $TENAGA (5347.MY)$ and $PCHEM (5183.MY)$ stood out as notable underperformers.
– Tenaga’s share price retreated by about 5% after its results, largely due to one-off impairments and cost-side pressures that weighed on near-term earnings growth.
– Petronas Chemicals, meanwhile, continues to face a soft global chemicals downcycle, narrower product spreads and inventory adjustments. Its share price slumped by more than 10% in a single session post-results, underscoring investor caution over its short-term earnings trajectory.
Why Did YTL Group Shares Plunge?
$YTL (4677.MY)$ and $YTLPOWR (6742.MY)$ both saw sharp pullbacks after FY2026 Q1 results fell short of expectations.
YTL Power reported revenue of RM5.36bn (down 6% YoY, third consecutive quarterly decline) with profit before tax at RM660m and net profit at RM485m (both down YoY), prompting an ~8% single-day drop. AI data centres remain in the investment phase with no near-term profit contribution.
Other Weak Spots: Tech Manufacturing and Gaming
Elsewhere, semiconductor OSAT (outsourced semiconductor assembly and test) and EMS (electronics manufacturing services) names such as $INARI (0166.MY)$ continued to grapple with slower-than-expected end-demand recovery and a prolonged inventory digestion cycle, leading to constrained order visibility and earnings pressure.
In the gaming and leisure space, operators like $GENM (4715.MY)$ have seen physical footfall recover, but earnings normalisation has lagged early post-pandemic hopes due to shifts in consumer spending patterns and regulatory considerations, leaving share prices lacking strong catalysts for now.
Market Outlook: Weakness as a Buying Opportunity
Looking ahead, most houses see Malaysian earnings as increasingly divergent but not structurally impaired, with the market likely to remain driven by stock and sector selection rather than a broad-based re-rating. Banks, construction and infrastructure, as well as building materials, together with plantations, are still viewed as the key pillars underpinning the FBM KLCI in the near term.
Although the $FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ has lagged regional peers by about 2–5 percentage points in recent months, HLIB argues that the latest pullback offers a buying opportunity, citing supportive valuation signals and the prospect of a Fed easing cycle narrowing the gap between the federal funds rate (FFR) and Bank Negara’s overnight policy rate (OPR), which could in turn aid foreign inflows and a stronger ringgit.
RHB Research, meanwhile, advocates a nimble approach, encouraging investors to look for opportunities in laggards during periods of share-price weakness, noting that a broadly stable global and domestic macro backdrop, clearer tariff and policy settings and easing US–China trade tensions should all help underpin the equity market into 2026.
Mooers, as we enter the final month of 2025, which sector's investment opportunities are you most bullish on? Share your views in the comments below!

title: In-depth Discussion on the GENM Acquisition Battle The moment Genting announced the acquisition of GENM, the battle for GENM's acquisition began. The business
author: 心如紫水
body:
In-depth Discussion on the GENM Acquisition Battle The moment Genting announced the acquisition of GENM, the battle for GENM's acquisition began. The business arena is akin to a battlefield. As Sun Tzu's Art of War states: 'Know yourself and know your enemy, and you will win a hundred battles out of a hundred.' It is crucial to clearly understand both your own strength and that of the opponent. If we consider Genting as the acquirer or the attacking party, then the minority shareholders of GENM are the defending side. This war has only one objective: GENM. Let us first list the cards held by both sides: Attacking Party: Genting Group Commander: TS Lim Khoon Thai Resources: 6 billion in cash, over 100 billion in Genting Group assets, top-tier advisors Morale: High, confident of success, already secured 50% of shares Defenders: Minority shareholders of GENM Commander: Leaderless Resources: None, fragmented forces, numerous unqualified advisors, self-proclaimed gurus Morale: Low, stubborn The attacking side needs to capture two key positions to take over GENM: the 75% threshold and the 90% threshold. Crossing the 75% threshold means they can apply for a trading halt, freezing all external support and completing the encirclement of remaining shareholders. Surpassing the 90% threshold implies the company can apply for delisting, allowing the major shareholder to act with impunity, effectively securing victory. Securing the 75% threshold is not particularly difficult. Please refer to my previous analysis:https://www.facebook.com/groups/1399899867001472/posts/4249352348722862/ This 75% is a confident estimate, but what about the remaining 25%? That’s hard to say, given that the offer price isn’t particularly high. As for how to reach the 90% threshold, capturing the leader first is key; this depends on who the main commander is. Commander: TS Lim Kok Thay, known for being meticulous and prudent in his approach, yet not hasty—this is evident to all. Given the commander's personality, shareholders should not expect any leniency or adjustments in the share price. Moreover, the commander is patient and unwilling to compromise, preferring to use a strategy of trading time for space to gradually acquire minority shareholders. Therefore, he can continuously employ tactics with frequent success. On the advisory side, besides having a highly professional Zhuge Liang-like strategist, there is also a team of traders calculating votes, and they can consult other financial tycoons for advice at any time. So, what strategies do minority shareholders have? Looking at the minority shareholders here, they are essentially retail investors. Institutional investors and large funds have long withdrawn their support, as they see the siege is complete and would not bother getting involved. The best strategy out of the Thirty-Six Stratagems is retreat. What about the major shareholders? Most of them are longstanding shareholders, and as long as they receive dividends, they don’t care about acquisition battles, defense, or resistance—essentially, as long as they get paid, they remain indifferent. In terms of advisors, there are only a group of incompetent strategists, and worse still, many unprofessional gurus (definitely not Tian Ge 😅). The resources available to them are minimal—they lack connections and resources, and worse, they operate independently with differing opinions and ideas every day. In this confrontation, one side is a professional army, while the other can be considered an irregular force. It goes without saying who will emerge victorious. Since the acquirer is unwilling to raise the price, they will need to think of operational maneuvers instead. What kind of moves? Based on past examples and the commander’s personality, it will likely involve a slow grind. Since it involves a slow grind, the acquirer will ensure that the acquisition does not exceed 75%, as exceeding that would mean game over and necessitate an official declaration. By keeping the acquisition below 75%, additional efforts can be made to show that the ownership has surpassed 73%, leaving just 1% short. This creates a Sword of Damocles hanging over each minority shareholder, putting them in a dilemma. Every day, they fear that the company might cross the 75% threshold, leading to a potential trading halt. Once trading halts, who will buy or sell shares? This is just the beginning. Don’t forget, the company has already announced the failure of the acquisition, but it’s only short by 1%. Consequently, market liquidity will significantly decrease, as no fund would want to purchase shares of a company nearing delisting or with such poor liquidity. In other words, currently, very few people are buying GENM shares, and those wanting to sell can only wait for the sole buyer to make a move. Yes, this is essentially a trading halt without an official suspension, but with an added disadvantage: after a suspension or delisting, the final trading price becomes the reference for transactions, fixing the price for buying and selling based on the last traded price. However, without an official suspension, the price can fluctuate freely each day, potentially falling like a free-falling object due to a lack of buyers supporting the stock price. The share price can slide from 2.35 to 2.25, then to 2.15, 2.05, 1.9, 1.8, 1.7, and so on, until one day you can’t bear it anymore and let go. Understand this: I’m not trying to scare anyone. The gap to that 1% won’t be far, so don’t expect funds or major shareholders to step in and sweep up shares—it’s highly unrealistic. If this situation persists over time, floating shares in the market will gradually flow toward the Genting Group, ensuring the acquirer's victory. Once the 90% threshold is crossed, the acquirer can apply for delisting and mandatory redemption, thereby completing the privatization. The timeline doesn’t matter; the commander’s personality dictates patience, and he is willing to wait indefinitely. After all, the acquirer has invested significant resources, spending MYR 6 billion on this battle and employing numerous top strategists, making success almost inevitable. What twists and turns might occur, or what new tactics the acquirer may deploy, remain to be seen. However, as the defending side, they can only endure the blows. Don’t ask me for ways to turn defeat into victory. There’s an English saying: Those that care don't know, those that know don't care 🤣😂😅

title: Why did Lim Kok Thay increase his equity stake from 66.16% to 73.15% on the last day instead of directly reaching 75%? And why is he continuing to slowly buy
author: 心如紫水
body: Why did Lim Kok Thay increase his equity stake from 66.16% to 73.15% on the last day instead of directly reaching 75%? And why is he continuing to slowly buy in the market? He wants the market to face reality! Earlier, when he offered a price of 2.35, many people complained it was too low, even demanding 2.6? 2.8? Or 3? However, he was able to purchase shares on the open market at a price as low as 2.18, which further dropped to 2.15, and now the share price is only around 2.2! His actions are meant to make the market realize that while dreams are beautiful, reality is harsh. Those who previously refused to sell at 2.35, would they reconsider selling if an offer of 2.35 were made again? Many didn't sell earlier and even bought at the bottom because at that time the stake was only 60%, and with one week left, many thought there was still a chance to fight! But what happened? On Friday it was 66.16%, and on the final day, Monday, it suddenly jumped to 73.13%! He is sending a message to the market: he still has ammunition in his gun! The idea of acquiring Genm isn’t something that emerged in just the past few months; it has been planned and laid out for several years. The current drop in the stock price to such a low level is no coincidence. Within the opposing camp of retail investors, how much of the shares does he hold that haven't been sold yet? Unknown? Previously, when Genm’s stock price fell to a low of 1.46, who do you think accumulated those shares at the bottom? Many believe that Lim Kok Thay's ultimate goal is to acquire up to 90% of the shares and then apply for a mandatory general offer. But I don’t think so. What he wants is simply that “as long as the opposition doesn’t exceed 10%, it’s considered approved!” Voter turnout is never 100%; participation above 95% is already considered very high. Some people feel their votes are insignificant and abstain, some forget to vote, others are confused, and some are “ghost shareholders” who remain completely inactive like ownerless spirits? If you don't oppose at the shareholders' meeting, your silence will be taken as consent! Once he reaches 75% control while public float remains below 25%, he can apply for a trading suspension. Typically, Bursa would give the company time to adjust its equity, but he won't need to! Earlier, Genting already stated that “once the acquisition reaches 75%, there is no intention to maintain the listing status,” meaning he might keep the stock suspended indefinitely. Suspension is not the same as delisting. If the shareholders’ meeting votes against the resolution, will Genm resume trading? It’s highly unlikely, as they have already stated they have no intention of maintaining the listing status. If they wanted to resume trading, they would need to sell down their holdings to below 75%. In my view, this is like meat buns thrown to dogs—there’s no turning back! Lim Kok Thay is likely to keep the stock suspended until the next offer. Retail investors won’t be able to sell, and no one will escape. During the suspension, they can only privately seek buyers themselves. If it fails the first time, the suspension could trap you for a year or more. Will you still have the same defiance the second time? What about the third or fourth attempt? Lim Kok Thay has plenty of strategies—he’ll use whichever suits him best! ... To be continued! #Repost

title: Foreign investors net bought Malaysian stocks worth MYR 11.6 million last week.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, August 8) Foreign investors ended two consecutive weeks of net selling, turning slightly net buyers of Malaysian stocks last week with net purchases amounting to MYR 11.6 million, compared to net sales of MYR 484.8 million the week before. Year-to-date, foreign capital outflows from Malaysia have totaled MYR 20.26 billion, significantly higher than the full-year net outflow of MYR 4.21 billion recorded last year. According to the latest fund flow report by Malacca Securities, foreign investors turned net sellers of Malaysian stocks again last Thursday and Friday, offloading MYR 80.3 million and MYR 172.3 million respectively. However, due to continuous inflows in the first three trading sessions, last week as a whole still saw net inflows. The sectors most favored by foreign investors last week were financial services (MYR 532 million), industrial products and services (MYR 83 million), and communications and media (MYR 58.6 million). Meanwhile, the sectors most heavily sold by foreign investors were utilities (-MYR 351.9 million), healthcare (-MYR 108.1 million), and technology (-MYR 86.7 million). On the other hand, local institutional investors were net buyers of Malaysian stocks last week, purchasing MYR 83 million worth, marking the second consecutive week of providing support to the market; however, retail investors turned to net selling, offloading MYR 94.6 million worth of Malaysian stocks last week. The average daily trading volume in the market last week generally declined, with trading activities of retail investors, local institutions, and foreign capital decreasing by 3.3%, 20.6%, and 28.8% respectively.
Top 10 stock purchases by foreign capital: $MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ , $CIMB (1023.MY)$ , $PMETAL (8869.MY)$ , $RHBBANK (1066.MY)$ , $TM (4863.MY)$ , $ALLIANZ (1163.MY)$ , $IOIPG (5249.MY)$$FFB (5306.MY)$ , $PBBANK (1295.MY)$ , $AMBANK (1015.MY)$
