rich_text.text: (Kuala Lumpur, August 8) Foreign capital ended two consecutive weeks of net selling and slightly net purchased MYR 11.6 million worth of Malaysian stocks last week, compared to a net sell of MYR 484.8 million the week before.
Year-to-date, foreign capital outflows have amounted to MYR 20.26 billion, significantly higher than the net outflow of MYR 4.21 billion for the whole of last year.

According to the latest fund flow report by MBSB, foreign investors turned net sellers again on Thursday and Friday last week, offloading MYR 80.3 million and MYR 172.3 million worth of Malaysian stocks respectively.
However, due to continuous inflows over the previous three trading sessions, last week as a whole still saw net inflows.

The sectors that were most favored by foreign investors last week were financial services (MYR 532 million), industrial products and services (MYR 83 million), and communications and media (MYR 58.6 million).
Meanwhile, the sectors with the largest sell-offs by foreign investors were utilities (-MYR 351.9 million), healthcare (-MYR 108.1 million), and technology (-MYR 86.7 million).

On the other hand, local institutional investors were net buyers of Malaysian stocks last week, purchasing MYR 83 million worth, marking the second consecutive week of supporting the market. However, retail investors turned to net selling, offloading MYR 94.6 million worth of Malaysian equities last week.

The average daily trading volume in the market declined across the board last week, with trading activities from retail investors, local institutional investors, and foreign investors falling sequentially by 3.3%, 20.6%, and 28.8%, respectively.

title: Slower profit recovery and rising debt risks lead Moody's to downgrade Genting's rating.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 9th news) International rating agency Moody's downgraded Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$ and its two subsidiaries—Genting Overseas Holdings and Genting Singapore. Moody's released the latest ratings while Genting was attempting to privatize Genting Malaysia through debt financing. $GENM (4715.MY)$at this time. According to Moody's statement, the ratings of Genting and Genting Overseas Holdings will be downgraded from Baa2 to Baa3, while the rating for Genting Singapore will be lowered from A3 to Baa1. The outlook for all three remains 'stable'. The agency noted: 'The downgrade of Genting’s ratings is mainly due to slower-than-expected profit recovery, prolonged constraints in deleveraging efforts, already weak financial conditions, and the additional financial burden from acquiring Genting Malaysia through debt financing. Moreover, further capital investment may still be required for the development of Resorts World New York, which will exacerbate financial pressures.' 'However, the stable outlook reflects our expectation that profitability in Singapore and Las Vegas will continue to improve, execution risks for the New York project remain manageable, and it is expected to start contributing profits by the second half of 2026, thereby improving the group’s credit metrics.' Moody's added that Genting’s standalone liquidity position remains robust, primarily supported by fees and dividends from its operating subsidiaries. Heavy debt pressure in 2027 However, Genting will face the pressure of debt maturity in 2027, including a USD 1.5 billion (approximately MYR 6.16 billion) note issued by Genting Overseas Holdings Capital, which is due in January 2027. Subsequently, a total of MYR 1.9 billion in debt from its subsidiaries, Genting RMTN Corporation and Genting Capital Corporation, will mature in March and June 2027, respectively. We expect Genting to refinance at least part of its upcoming maturing debt within the next 6 to 12 months. Last week, CreditSights, a credit research firm under Fitch, also warned that both Genting and Genting Malaysia face the risk of rating downgrades due to their high debt levels and pressured cash flows. Previously, Moody's had placed Genting on its rating watch list in October, pending the outcome of the full acquisition of Genting Malaysia. As of early December, Genting’s privatization offer has expired, during which it acquired 73.133% of Genting Malaysia’s shares, but the privatization was unsuccessful.

The Waiting Period and The Constraint
Under Malaysia's takeover rules (specifically the Rules on Take-Overs, Mergers and Compulsory Acquisitions):
1. The Key Restriction: The 12-Month Rule
An offeror (Genting Berhad) whose bid has failed to meet the required threshold is restricted from acquiring more than 2% of the target's shares (GENM) within 12 months of the closing of the previous offer.
Previous Offer Closure Date: December 1, 2025.
Start of Restriction: December 2, 2025.
Restriction End Date: December 1, 2026.
This 12-month restriction is the most immediate roadblock to a quick second attempt.

title: As 'Visit Malaysia 2026' Approaches, What Are the Potential Investment Opportunities?
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
The upcoming "Visit Malaysia 2026" (VM2026) campaign is set to become a key engine driving the recovery of the country’s diversified economy. Its impact is expected to extend across multiple sectors. According to data from the Department of Statistics Malaysia, tourism currently contributes over 15% to the nation’s GDP, and this share is projected to increase further by 2026.
Building on this robust foundation, the government has set ambitious targets for VM2026: to attract more than 47 million international visitors and generate approximately RM329 billion in tourism revenue. To support the campaign, the government will allocate a substantial RM500 million for promotion and incentives, including tax relief for tourism operators.
The campaign is expected to spur significant growth in a range of related industries, with key beneficiaries including aviation, hotel accommodation, medical tourism, gaming, food and beverage, and real estate investment trusts (REITs).
Aviation
The restructured aviation ecosystem is a direct catalyst for tourism growth. Capital A $CAPITALA (5099.MY)$ has transitioned from a pure airline operator to a “travel and lifestyle platform,” having transferred its core airline operations to its subsidiary, AirAsia X $AAX (5238.MY)$ . This strategic move allows AAX to emerge as a unified, scaled airline entity well-positioned to capture the surge in medium and long-haul travel demand.According to the latest quarterly report, AAX’s 25Q3 revenue reached RM803.5 million, reflecting a slight YoY increase. The passenger load factor (PLF) remained healthy at 82%. The average base fare increased by 5% year-on-year to RM466 in Q3 2025, as market demand built up towards the upcoming peak travel season. Investors can view Capital A for its diversified exposure to travel-related digital and logistics services, while AAX offers a more direct play on international air travel recovery.
Gaming and Integrated Resorts
The recovery of tourism is crucial for Malaysia's gaming industry revenue, which relies heavily on foreign visitors. Genting Malaysia $GENM (4715.MY)$ derives over 40% of its income from international tourists, with its resort in Genting Highlands serving as an integrated destination combining hotels, amusement parks, shopping, and gaming, where a rebound in visitor numbers would directly boost its overall performance. As a holding company, Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$ operates across a broader business spectrum, and the overall increase in tourism activity driven by a travel boom similarly benefits its integrated resort operations.
Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)
REITs that own prime retail and commercial assets in tourist-frequented locations offer a stable avenue to generate income from the tourism boom. Analysts highlight that REITs like Pavilion REIT $PAVREIT (5212.MY)$ continue to benefit from the tourism rebound, with its flagship Pavilion Kuala Lumpur mall being a major draw. Similarly, $SUNREIT (5176.MY)$ (with assets like Sunway Pyramid) and KLCC REIT $KLCC (5235SS.MY)$ (owner of the Suria KLCC mall beneath the Petronas Twin Towers) are strategically positioned in iconic locations. These REITs benefit not just from retail sales but also from hospitality segments within their integrated developments.
Consumer Staples & Food & Beverage
The tourism wave will also lift consumption across everyday retail and dining channels. Brewers like Heineken Malaysia $HEIM (3255.MY)$ and Carlsberg Malaysia $CARLSBG (2836.MY)$ are highlighted by analysts to continue benefiting from the economic reopening, with potential uplifts from the return of international visitors and resilient domestic demand. Their products are staples in restaurants, bars, and hotels nationwide. Furthermore, a company like Oriental Kopi $KOPI (0338.MY)$ , with its widespread network of cafes strategically located in transportation hubs and urban centers, is ideally positioned to serve the daily needs of both tourists and locals, making it a subtle yet direct beneficiary of increased foot traffic. $99SMART (5326.MY)$ $NESTLE (4707.MY)$
Medical Tourism
Malaysia’s reputation as a center for high-quality, affordable healthcare represents a synergistic investment niche alongside tourism. Medical tourism revenue is a significant contributor for major healthcare groups. Healthcare providers such as $IHH (5225.MY)$ and $KPJ (5878.MY)$ derive about 7-15% of their revenue from medical tourists. These healthcare providers, with their strategic geographic presence and state-of-the-art facilities, are particularly well-placed to capture pent-up demand from returning international patients seeking elective and specialized procedures. The sector offers a defensive growth angle tied to longer tourist stays and higher-value spending. $ALPHA (0303.MY)$
Positioning for a Macroeconomic Tailwind
The “Visit Malaysia 2026” campaign is more than a marketing initiative; it is a coordinated national strategy expected to act as a key engine for macroeconomic growth. For investors, this creates a multi-sector opportunity. From the direct leverage of airlines and resorts to the steady, property-backed dividends of REITs and the broad-based consumption lift for F&B and retail, the upcoming tourism wave is set to ripple through the Malaysian economy. While individual stock performance will vary based on execution and valuation, the overarching trend provides a strong tailwind for strategically positioned companies, making 2026 a pivotal year for Malaysia’s markets and its economic narrative.

🇺🇸Wall Street Summary
$S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ 6,800.26 (-0.24%)
$Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ 48,114.26 (-0.62%)
$Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ 23,111.46 (+0.23%)
US stocks were mixed Tuesday: the $Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ edged up 0.2% while the $S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ fell 0.2% and the $Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ slid 0.6%. Tech outperformed as $Tesla (TSLA.US)$ jumped 3.1% to a record close on robotaxi momentum, and Palantir, Oracle, and Meta advanced.
The Dow lagged on weakness in healthcare, with $Johnson & Johnson (JNJ.US)$, $UnitedHealth (UNH.US)$, and $Merck & Co (MRK.US)$ retreating.
A mixed jobs update (Nov +64k vs. 45k expected; Oct -105k) stoked hopes for a January Fed rate cut but also raised growth concerns.
Crypto rose on rate-cut bets: $Bitcoin (BTC.CC)$ +2.1% to 87,686, $Ethereum (ETH.CC)$ +0.7% to 2,951, $Solana (SOL.CC)$ +2.8% to 128.34, and $Ripple (XRP.CC)$ +2.4% to 1.93.
🇲🇾Bursa Market Insight
$FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ 1,648.31 (+0.28%)
Top Gainer: $99SMART (5326.MY)$ RM3.65 (+2.82%)
Top Loser: $QL (7084.MY)$ RM3.95 (-1.00%)
USD/MYR: $USD/MYR (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.0855 (-0.17%)
Bursa Malaysia extended its winning streak to four sessions, with the $FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ up 0.28% to 1,648.31. Activity picked up, but market breadth was weak as decliners topped gainers.
Financial heavyweights led the rise, supported by a resilient domestic backdrop, easier global conditions after the Fed’s rate cut, and year-end rebalancing that favored large-cap defensives. Turnover increased to 2.59 billion shares worth RM2.27 billion.
CIMB Securities' sectoral analysis shows the financial services sector commands 25% of Bursa Malaysia's total market capitalisation (RM474 billion) despite representing just 3.4% of listings (37 securities) as of Dec 12, 2025. By contrast, industrial and consumer products each account for about 12% of market value despite large listing counts.
Other heavyweights include utilities (9%), plantations (8%), and telecommunications (7%), followed by healthcare (6%), property (5%), and technology and construction (4% each).
Smaller sectors like transportation and logistics, REITs, and energy contribute 2–3%, while ETFs and trusts are negligible.
🔍IPO Scanner
🔔Stocks to Watch
$VELESTO (5243.MY)$ will sell its Naga 3 jack-up rig for US$63 million (RM258.4 million) to streamline its fleet. It expects a RM17.1 million gain and plans to use RM251.1 million for shareholder payouts, corporate needs and working capital by December 2026.
New York's gaming commission unanimously approved casino licences for $GENM (4715.MY)$, Bally's Bronx and Hard Rock Metropolitan Park, ending a decade-long process. Governor Kathy Hochul said the projects must honor community commitments; the vote followed Dec 1 recommendations.
$UWC (5292.MY)$'s 1QFY2026 net profit rose to RM17.1 million from RM6.49 million as revenue hit a record RM120.84 million, up 35%. The group is upbeat on semiconductor recovery and AI-driven demand.
$APOLLO (6432.MY)$'s 2QFY2026 net profit fell 30% y-o-y to RM7.45 million, with revenue down 2.7% to RM75.26 million on weaker sales and higher costs. It expects stabilisation after overhauling its distribution model.
$CYPARK (5184.MY)$ reported a 2QFY2026 net loss of RM15.54 million versus a RM2.28 million profit a year ago; excluding last year's one-off, losses widened from RM8.9 million. Revenue slipped to RM46.19 million, but the group sees better visibility from LSS5+ and SMART WTE Phase 2 nearing approval.
$PTT (7010.MY)$ won a RM35.88 million contract from Sime Darby Property for earthworks at Bandar Bukit Raja Business Park in Kapar, Klang. Work starts Jan 5, 2026, and ends Sept 4, 2027.
$CARIMIN (5257.MY)$ secured a RM33.98 million fixed-price contract from $PETGAS (6033.MY)$ to replace the gas pipeline linked to the Putra Heights explosion. Its unit Carimin Engineering Services will handle procurement, construction and commissioning.
$MSNIAGA (5011.MY)$ landed a RM19.82 million, 65-month lease-to-use deal from the Education Ministry to supply IT equipment to schools in northern Sarawak from Jan 2026 to May 2031. The scope covers laptops, printers, projectors and charging carts, with no automatic renewal.

title: High capital expenditures impact financial metrics; S&P downgrades Genting Group's outlook to 'negative'.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 18th) S&P Global Ratings announced that it has revised the outlook for Genting Group and several of its core subsidiaries from 'stable' to 'negative'.
According to S&P Global Ratings' statement yesterday, the downgrade reflects potential downward pressure on Genting Group’s credit quality over the next two to three years due to high capital expenditures and an aggressive expansion strategy.
However, the long-term issuer and debt ratings for the relevant entities remain unchanged.
The companies affected by the revised outlook include Genting, $GENTING (3182.MY)$Genting Malaysia, $GENM (4715.MY)$ Genting New York, and Genting Las Vegas.
S&P noted that Genting Group will concurrently advance several large-scale investment plans in the coming years, including:
· Follow-up investments by Genting New York after obtaining a full casino license in New York State;
· Expansion project of Resorts World Sentosa in Singapore;
· Genting Energy's investment in a Floating Liquefied Natural Gas (FLNG) facility in Indonesia;
· The parent company proposed a privatization acquisition plan for Genting Malaysia worth approximately MYR 3.1 billion.
Driven by the aforementioned projects, S&P Global Ratings estimates that Genting Group’s capital expenditure in 2026 may reach twice the amount of approximately MYR 6 billion projected for 2025, significantly higher than the MYR 4.3 billion in 2024. It is also expected that annual capital expenditure will remain above MYR 8 billion from 2026 to 2030.
Among these, investments related to the New York casino license are expected to account for nearly 30% of the group's annual capital expenditure over the next two to three years, covering license fees, renovations of existing facilities, and the construction of new facilities.
Meanwhile, the renovation plan for Resorts World Sentosa in Singapore will continue until 2030, while the FLNG project in Indonesia will last at least until 2027, further increasing overall investment levels.
New revenue generation struggles to keep pace with expenditures.
S&P Global believes that new earnings will struggle to fully keep pace with the growth in expenditures. Although the pre-tax annual contribution from the New York project is expected to exceed USD 400 million (approximately MYR 1.64 billion) in the long term, the FLNG project is unlikely to generate cash flow until the middle of 2027 at the earliest.
The recovery of the Singapore operations will also require substantial capital investment, which could weaken the group’s cash buffer.
In an environment of high capital expenditure, S&P Global anticipates that Genting’s free cash flow will remain negative over the next three years, with total group debt potentially increasing from MYR 21 billion in 2024 to approximately MYR 35 billion by 2028.
Under such circumstances, a key metric for measuring deleveraging capacity — the FFO-to-debt ratio — could fall below 20% during 2026–2027, below the ideal threshold for investment-grade ratings.
S&P Global noted that Genting Group’s growth-oriented strategy deviates from its prior expectations for maintaining an investment-grade credit profile, and the group currently lacks a clear financial policy framework.
“Particularly as rating headroom narrows, continuing to pursue acquisitions and expansion through debt financing increases financial uncertainty.”
Credit rating remains unchanged
Nevertheless, S&P Global has maintained the group’s current rating, primarily due to the positive impact of the New York casino license on long-term competitiveness.
The report highlights that Genting holds a near-monopoly position in New York’s downstate gaming market over the next three to four years. The region’s dense population, high income levels, and robust tourism demand are expected to support Genting New York’s operational performance.
The business generated nearly USD 1 billion (approximately MYR 4.1 billion) in annual gross gaming revenue in 2023 and 2024, with relatively stable operating performance.
In addition, S&P Global expects that as the expansion of Resorts World Sentosa progresses and operations at Genting Las Vegas recover following management adjustments, the group's other gaming businesses are likely to improve gradually.
The group’s adjusted pre-tax profit for the third quarter of 2025 was approximately MYR 2.2 billion, an increase from the average level of the previous two quarters.
Looking ahead, S&P Global stated that if Genting Group fails to demonstrate sufficient financial discipline during a high-investment cycle, resulting in operating cash flow-to-debt ratios remaining below 20% over the long term, a further downgrade is not ruled out.
Conversely, if the group implements a clear deleveraging and refinancing plan, or if the New York project performs better than expected, there is still potential for the rating outlook to stabilize.
Source: Nanyang Business Daily

#wastedpatience #falseconviction #adaptability
For me 2025 is definitely a hard year to swallow. With just a meagre 2% return that cant even beat inflation!

with over almost one third of my holdings in $GENM (4715.MY)$ , I have been patient holding on to this stock with the conviction that this company will have a recovery of earnings in 2025 which they did in certain quarters but that fail to ignite a rally in their share price. Still me being me, strongly believe that this company is fundamentally strong, i continue to hold on but the biggest bomb failed with the news of their privatisation effort. Yet i did not take up the offer as i believed that the take over price of 2.30 is too undervalued keeping in mind they have about to win the new york state casino license. And once that deadline is over and they did win the license, you would expect the price should react positively but no, it went down and down and yet I still hold on. 🤣
2) adaptability
hence for 2026 my promise to myself is that if the price still depressed i would shift all or a big portion away. had i not hold on to it and diverted into my USA holdings like google which i have now almost 50% gain, my return would be so much better. this year i will focus on this strategy: Malaysia holdings focusing on stable companies that provide decent dividends and using those dividends to funnel into my growth engine stock and winners like $Invesco S&P 500 Momentum Etf (SPMO.US)$ and $Alphabet-C (GOOG.US)$ and $Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT.US)$ . any dividends from US stock holdings will also be directed into spmo.
and hopefully 2026 will be a better year!

title: 📊 Changes in the Top 30 Market Cap of Malaysia's Stock Market
author: 理财嘛嘛档
body: It has been less than two years since I last recorded the top 30 companies by market capitalization in Malaysia as of May 21, 2024, but we can already notice significant changes in the rankings. Regulars like the top 30 $GENM (4715.MY)$ , $GENTING (3182.MY)$ have been knocked out of the top 30 rankings. Two of my dividend stocks, $UTDPLT (2089.MY)$ and $WPRTS (5246.MY)$ have quietly squeezed into the top 30, while others such as $TIMECOM (5031.MY)$ , $IGBREIT (5227.MY)$ , $SUNREIT (5176.MY)$ are still within the top 50. $MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ 、 $PBBANK (1295.MY)$ 、 $CIMB (1023.MY)$ still hold steady in the top ranks; a particularly eye-catching change is RHB significantly overtaking others to climb to 12th place. Upon closer inspection, you'll find that most large-cap stocks with decent dividend yields have performed quite well over the past year, whereas the market downturn has mainly affected smaller-cap stocks. This proves that retail participation in the market remains minimal... For instance, among the 30 dividend stocks I track regularly, as many as 25 are among the top 200 companies by market capitalization in Malaysia, which also explains why their performance has stood out in recent years. title: 47 million tourists are coming 🔥 Is it too late for travel-related stocks?
author: Yuan TJ
body:
Lately, many people have been talking about: “Will the index go up?” “Is it still worth buying bank stocks?” But there’s one topic quietly gaining momentum —
👉 Malaysia Tourism Boom 🌏 And this time, it’s not just a recovery. It’s an upgraded era of tourism. 🌴 Why has travel suddenly become so appealing? Let me start with a fact. Have you noticed in the past couple of years — Airports are packed ✈️ Hotels are hard to book 🏨 Crowds are back at the malls 🛍️ Travel is no longer just weekend getaways. It's becoming a national economic engine. VMY2026 is not just a slogan. It’s a combination of long-term exposure, infrastructure development, and publicity. When the government gets serious about promoting something, Companies start making serious money. ✈️ The first layer of beneficiaries: airline stocks $CAPITALA (5099.MY)$ What is the first step for tourists coming to Malaysia? Taking a flight. Increase in flights, expansion of routes, and higher passenger load factors. Airlines naturally become the 'first to collect money.' As tourism热度 continues, the profit elasticity of airline stocks will be amplified. This is why, within the tourism theme, airlines are always the most direct concept stocks. 🏨 Second-tier beneficiaries: Hotels + REITs $SHANG (5517.MY)$
$PAVREIT (5212.MY)$
$YTLREIT (5109.MY)$ Tourists can't possibly sleep at the airport. Higher occupancy rates, Housing prices have pricing power, Catering consumption has increased. The benefits of REITs are —— ✔️ Generates cash flow ✔️ Provides distributions ✔️ Backed by assets As tourism rebounds, Hotel REITs usually benefit gradually. Not a sudden surge type, But a steady upward trend. 🎰 Third-tier benefit: Entertainment + Integrated Resorts $SPRITZER (7103.MY)$
$GENM (4715.MY)$
$OWG (5260.MY)$ Tourists don't come here just to sleep. They come to: 🎢 Play 🎰 Be entertained 🍽️ Eat 🛍️ Shop The strongest aspect of the integrated resort model is —— A single tourist, Can complete all their spending in one location. This is the 'consumption multiplier.' 🏥 Don't overlook medical tourism $SUNWAY (5211.MY)$ Many people only think of beaches and cuisine. But what holds truly high value is medical tourism. These travelers: Stay longer Spend more Often travel with family members This type of high-quality customer base benefits hotels, dining, and transportation alike. And this is a long-term structural trend. 🥤 Hidden Winners: Consumer Stocks More tourists, More bottled water sold 💧 Restaurants are busier 🍜 Malls are more bustling 🛍️ You might think it's just travel stocks on the rise, But in fact, many consumer stocks will also be driven up. Sometimes, The real money-makers are the 'less obvious companies'. 🧠 The investment logic is simple Tourism growth → More flights → Higher occupancy → More entertainment → Increased spending → More corporate profits When profitability improves, Valuations will naturally be repriced. The focus is not on hyping concepts. But on the earnings trajectory. ⚠️ Of course, there are risks as well Global economy Exchange rate fluctuations Regional competition All of these factors will influence tourism sentiment. But as long as the trend is upward, The thematic logic remains intact. 🎯 Malaysian investors need to ask themselves Is this round of tourism activity a short-term hype? Or does it represent a multi-year structural upgrade? When national-level initiatives continue to push forward, Companies have already started positioning themselves, Are you willing to wait until everyone understands before researching? 😏

title: Foreign Funds Net Inflows up RM411M as Money Fled Asia but Poured into Malaysia
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
The first week of March saw adramatic turnaround in Malaysian equities. After weeks of selling, global funds reversed course and poured money back in, even as a gloomy global backdrop triggered a widespread sell-off across Asia. While most indices fell, $FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ stood out as the only major global index to post a weekly gain. Let's dive into where the money flowed in this contrasting environment.
Market Pulse: Cracks Emerge in the U.S. Labor Market
The big shock came from the U.S., where nonfarm payrolls fell by 92k in February, marking the largest decline infour months. This, coupled with softer retail sales and PMI data, fueled recession worries. Among 20 major indices tracked, only Malaysia's FBM KLCI eked out a 0.1% gain. Others weren't so lucky, with $Korea Composite Index (.KOSPI.KR)$ plunging 10.6% and $Nikkei 225 (.N225.JP)$ tumbling 5.5%. Oil prices surged over 20% due to Middle East tensions, while the US dollar strengthened against most currencies, including the Ringgit.
Asia's Money Moves: The USD14.8B Flight from Asian Equities
Across the eight Asian markets monitored, foreign investors were net sellers for the third week in a row,pulling out a massive -USD14.83 billion. The selling was widespread, led by Korea (-USD3.21b), India (-USD2.29b), Thailand (-USD423.5m), Vietnam (-USD234.8m), and the Philippines (-USD16.2m). High oil prices and domestic inflation concerns drove the exodus. Notably, only Indonesia and Malaysia managed to attract net foreign inflows amidst the regional turmoil.
Malaysia Breakdown: A Lone Bright Spot
Malaysia's market told a different story. Foreign investors ended a two-week selling streak, becoming net buyers to the tune of RM411.4 million. They were buyers on four out of five trading days. In contrast, local institutions extended their net selling to a fifth consecutive week, offloading -RM408.3m. Local retailers also turned cautious, snapping their two-week buying streak to record a small net outflow of -RM3.1m. Trading activity picked up, with the average daily volume for local retailers and institutions rising by about 18%, while foreign investor activity dipped by -14.6%.
Stock Spotlight: Who’s Buying What?
Strategy Breakdown: A Clash of Agendas
Foreigners' Top Picks: Their money chased large-cap, high-yield, and defensive names. Top net buys were $MISC (3816.MY)$ (Transportation, RM186.9m), $PCHEM (5183.MY)$ (RM167.4m), and $PBBANK (1295.MY)$ (RM162.4m), showing a preference for stable giants.
Local Institutions' Top Picks: They favored financials and construction, buying $MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ (RM103.0m), $GAMUDA (5398.MY)$ (RM86.8m), and $TM (4863.MY)$ (RM76.7m).
Local Retailers' Top Picks: They chased momentum and speculative names, with $AAX (5238.MY)$ (RM76.4m), $ZETRIX (0138.MY)$ (RM22.0m), and $GENM (4715.MY)$ (RM21.4m) topping their buy list.
Risks to Watch
Investors should stay vigilant. The primary risk remains global market volatility spilling over, especially if U.S. economic data continues to disappoint. Surging oil prices, while beneficial for Malaysia's exports, could dampen global growth and corporate earnings elsewhere, affecting sentiment. Domestically, the divergence between foreign and local institutional flows could lead to increased market choppiness. Finally, any escalation in geopolitical tensions remains a key wildcard.

title: My experience as a retail investor
author: DarthPuppyTheWise
body:
Embarking on the journey of investing just six months ago has been an insightful experience. My focus on swing trading has introduced a dynamic approach to the market. The learning curve has been steep, with earnings demonstrating a mixed performance so far. It is a continuous process of refinement and adaptation.
Navigating through periods of market volatility (during war) can be quite challenging, especially when it impacts core holdings. It is understandable to question your conviction during such times. However, maintaining a long-term perspective is often beneficial for investment success. Trusting the underlying principles and the potential for future growth can help in weathering these storms. Focusing on the long-term prospect is a prudent approach.
I'm currently restructuring my investment strategy to better suit my long-term goals. This involves allocating funds for enduring holdings, while also dedicating some capital to shorter-term trading opportunities. Additionally, I'm taking steps to address and learn from previous trading decisions that didn't quite pan out. It's a multi-faceted approach to improve overall portfolio performance. This comprehensive plan aims for more consistent and positive results moving forward.

body: 🚀 4715 GENM Analysis – The Casino King Reclaims RM 2.00! Can it Gamble Through the RM 2.10 Wall? 🎲 Genting Malaysia is making a bold move this Monday morning (April 27, 2026), trading at RM 2.060 (+0.98%). After months of sideways grinding, the stock is finally showing signs of life, slicing through major psychological and technical barriers. 📈 1. Price Trend: The Structural Shift Status: Major Breakout. GENM has officially reclaimed the critical Weekly MA30 (RM 2.024). Trading above this line on a weekly basis usually signals a transition from a "Bear Market" to a "Bullish Recovery." Daily Momentum: The price is gapping away from the EMA5 (RM 1.984) and EMA10 (RM 1.936). The slope is vertical, indicating strong buying urgency. Volume Ratio: 4.03. 🔥 Extreme Conviction. Volume is over 4x higher than the average morning session. This confirms that this isn't just a retail "flutter"—this is institutional repositioning. 🌊 2. Money Flow: Institutions Leading the Charge 📊 The "Smart Money" is clearly fueling this move: Net Inflow: +RM 847.13k (Intraday). 🟢 Solid positive accumulation. Large (L) Players: +RM 216k Net Inflow. 🐋 Institutional mid-tier funds are active buyers today. Medium (M) Players: +RM 531k Net Inflow. This segment is the primary engine of today's price surge. XL Whales: 0.00 Inflow. The "Super Jerungs" are staying quiet for now, likely waiting for the RM 2.10 resistance to be tested before committing heavy capital. The Verdict: A healthy rally driven by mid-to-large tier funds. Retail is participating (+RM 99k) but is not the main driver. 🧱 3. Order Book: The RM 2.10 "Boss Level" Bid/Ask Ratio: 42.04% Bids vs 57.96% Asks. 🚨 The sellers are currently stacking up to cap the rally. The Ceiling: There is a massive "Great Wall" at RM 2.100 (531.6k shares). This is the ultimate hurdle for the day. The Support Floor: Buyers are grouped at RM 2.040 (184k shares). This level acted as the launchpad this morning and must hold to maintain bullish momentum. ⚡ 4. Technical Sentiment: "Running Hot" Profit Ratio: 38.71%. 🚨 CRITICAL DATA. Only 38% of holders are currently in profit. The Average Cost is RM 2.100. This means the RM 2.10 level is not just technical resistance—it is the point where the majority of shareholders will try to "break even." Expect heavy selling pressure there. Weekly KDJ: J-line at 104.9. 🚨 Nuclear Overbought. On a weekly timeframe, the J-line crossing 100 is a major warning of a potential "Fast Pullback" or a sideways breather. MACD: 🟢 The Daily MACD histogram is expanding (+0.053), confirming the trend reversal is still accelerating. 🎯 5. DUAL TRADING PERSPECTIVES 🛡️ CONSERVATIVE PLAN (The Breakout Waiter) Logic: Respect the 104 J-line and the heavy supply at RM 2.10. Wait for a retest of the breakout point. Entry Zone: RM 1.980 – RM 2.020 (Buying the dip toward the Weekly MA30). Stop Loss: RM 1.920. Take Profit: RM 2.100 / RM 2.220. ⚡ RISK-TOLERANT PLAN (The Wall Squeezer) Logic: Betting on the 4.03 Volume Ratio to sweep the RM 2.10 wall before the closing bell. Entry Zone: RM 2.050 – RM 2.070. Stop Loss: RM 2.010. Take Profit: RM 2.150 / RM 2.200. ⚠️ Final Insight: GENM has successfully shifted its trend, but it is hitting a "Supply Minefield" at RM 2.10. With 61% of holders still in a loss, every move up will be met with "stuck" sellers exiting. Watch the volume at RM 2.10—if it doesn't spike to 10M+, expect a retreat. Are you betting on a RM 2.10 breakout today, or are you waiting for the overbought KDJ to cool down?

title: GENM — Low-volume support rebound, but still below key trend ceiling Key Highlights GENM is showing a small rebound from support, not a confirmed breakout.
author: TPkawkaw_MY
body: GENM — Low-volume support rebound, but still below key trend ceiling Key Highlights GENM is showing a small rebound from support, not a confirmed breakout. Price is holding around RM1.88–RM1.90, but still below stronger resistance near RM1.94. Money flow is mildly positive, but volume is still low, so momentum is not strong yet. Latest news flow may create uncertainty, especially the debt-funded New York project and possible Bimini sale angle. Price Action Daily chart shows GENM still in a sideways-to-weak recovery phase. Price is below MA10/MA20/MA30 area, meaning the trend has not fully turned bullish. Current support zone: RM1.84–RM1.88 Key resistance zone: RM1.92–RM1.94 A stronger breakout only looks cleaner if GENM can close above RM1.94. Money Flow Net inflow is small at around RM129.7K. XL shows inflow while no XL outflow is shown, which is mildly positive. But total volume ratio is only 0.74, so this is more like quiet support buying, not aggressive accumulation. Order Book Bid side is strong at 81.09%, suggesting buyers are defending the RM1.88 area. Ask wall is relatively thin: RM1.89: 62.7K RM1.90: 20K RM1.91: 20.1K RM1.92: 37.2K This means if buying volume appears, RM1.90–RM1.92 can be cleared quite easily. But the real test remains RM1.94. Technical Signals RSI around 42–49: neutral-to-weak, not overbought. KDJ J is very low around 2.9, meaning short-term rebound is possible. MACD daily is still negative, so trend momentum is not confirmed. 15m MACD is also weak, suggesting GENM needs stronger buying follow-through. Trading Plan Aggressive entry: RM1.88–RM1.90, only if RM1.88 continues to hold. Safer entry: above RM1.92 with better volume. Confirmation entry: above RM1.94, as this clears the main resistance from the market position overview. Cut-Loss Zone Tight cut-loss: below RM1.87 Wider cut-loss: below RM1.84 Take-Profit Zones TP1: RM1.92–RM1.94 TP2: RM1.98–RM2.00 Final View GENM is currently a support-rebound setup, not a breakout setup yet. The order book looks supportive and the ask side is light, but the weak volume and negative daily MACD mean confirmation is still missing. For a cleaner swing trade, GENM needs to reclaim RM1.92–RM1.94 with stronger volume. Is RM1.88 becoming a defended base, or is GENM still being capped below RM1.94? Disclaimer: For educational sharing only. Not a buy or sell call.

title: GENM is attempting to bounce from its 52-week low, but this remains a bottom-fishing setup—not yet a confirmed trend reversal. Stock Trend GENM remains in a
author: TPkawkaw_MY
body: GENM is attempting to bounce from its 52-week low, but this remains a bottom-fishing setup—not yet a confirmed trend reversal. Stock Trend GENM remains in a clear daily and weekly downtrend. The structure still shows lower highs and lower lows, with price falling from above RM2.00 toward the RM1.70 support zone. Both higher timeframes fail the Stage-2/A+ trend filter: Daily MACD remains below zero with DIF below DEA. Weekly MACD is also bearish and still deteriorating. Price has not formed a confirmed higher low or reclaimed any meaningful resistance. The small rebound from RM1.70 to RM1.71 is therefore an early reversal attempt, not a confirmed bullish reversal. Intraday momentum has improved slightly. RSI has recovered to around the neutral 47–55 range, while the 5-minute MACD is flattening near zero. This suggests selling pressure is temporarily easing, but buying momentum remains weak. Estimated Operator Cost Zone The broader cost concentration is around RM1.88, which also acts as major overhead resistance. Only around 1.1% of positions are currently profitable, meaning most holders remain trapped above the present price. The practical short-term zones are: RM1.70–RM1.72: immediate bottom-testing area RM1.76–RM1.80: first recovery supply zone RM1.85–RM1.88: major trapped-holder and cost resistance GENM will likely face selling pressure on any rebound because many holders may use higher prices to reduce exposure. Operator Plan Oversight GENM appears to be undergoing a possible selling-climax test near RM1.70, but accumulation has not yet been confirmed. The stronger volume during the recent decline suggests capitulation or forced selling may have occurred. However, daily money flow remains negative, with approximately RM256,000 net outflow and a much larger recent outflow bar visible in the historical flow. Medium-sized trades show some buying interest, but small-order selling continues to dominate. This could indicate early bargain hunting while weaker holders continue exiting. For a credible operator accumulation phase, GENM needs to hold RM1.70 repeatedly, show declining selling volume and begin recording consistent net inflow. Bid/Ask Strength The visible order book is strongly bid-heavy at approximately 85% bid versus 15% ask. Important levels include: RM1.70: approximately 760,000 shares waiting RM1.71: approximately 138,000 shares offered RM1.72: approximately 144,000 shares offered RM1.73: approximately 220,000 shares offered This provides immediate support, but the bid wall must be treated cautiously. A genuine reversal requires actual buying transactions lifting the offers, not merely large passive queues at RM1.70. Trap Risk The main risk is a dead-cat bounce from the 52-week low. GENM may briefly rebound toward RM1.74–RM1.80 before trapped holders sell into strength. Warning signs would include: RM1.70 bid support disappearing suddenly Repeated failure to clear RM1.72–RM1.73 A rebound occurring on weak volume Continued daily net outflow A close below RM1.70 A breakdown below RM1.70 would invalidate the immediate bottoming attempt and could expose RM1.65, followed by the broader RM1.55–RM1.60 region. Support and Resistance Immediate support: RM1.70 Secondary support: RM1.65–RM1.68 Major support: RM1.55–RM1.60 Immediate resistance: RM1.72–RM1.73 Recovery resistance: RM1.76–RM1.80 Major resistance: RM1.85–RM1.88 Trading Plan For an aggressive reversal trade, trader may observe whether GENM continues holding RM1.70 and breaks above RM1.72–RM1.73 with increasing volume. A safer entry requires GENM to: Recover above RM1.76. Form a higher low above RM1.70. Break RM1.80 with stronger buying volume and improved money flow. Possible risk plan: Aggressive entry: RM1.71–RM1.73 after confirmation Safer entry: above RM1.76–RM1.80 Tight cut-loss: below RM1.69 Wider swing cut-loss: below RM1.65 TP1: RM1.76–RM1.80 TP2: RM1.85–RM1.88 The risk-to-reward is acceptable only when the RM1.70 floor remains intact. Averaging down without reversal confirmation remains high risk because the weekly trend is still bearish. Final View GENM is showing an early technical rebound attempt at major support, supported by a strong visible bid queue and recovering intraday RSI. However, the daily and weekly trends remain bearish, MACD has not reversed and money flow still shows distribution. GENM is presently suitable only for a controlled speculative rebound trade, not yet a high-confidence swing setup. The first genuine improvement comes above RM1.76, while a stronger reversal signal requires RM1.80 to be reclaimed and held. Will RM1.70 become GENM’s accumulation floor, or merely another temporary stop in the ongoing downtrend? Not financial advice. Trade according to personal risk tolerance.

title: Honest advice is hard to hear
author: Kian Capital
body:
You guys are still holding out hope for this stock. The controlling shareholder attempted to take it private a year ago, but the plan fell through. This signals that the major shareholder doesn't want retail investors participating. I held this position for four years (2022-2025) and made zero profit, enduring daily agony as it declined more often than it rose. During this period, I averaged down several times to lower my cost basis. Just as they announced a share buyback, I managed to break even at 2.25 and exited.
I hope my lengthy ramblings can help those who are meant to find this avoid losing money unnecessarily here. As you can see in the chart above, I was relieved to have exited during the sideways consolidation phase because they were unable to accumulate enough shares. In the chart below, they resumed self-driven price increases to distribute shares around April or May of this year, and this trend has continued until now.

body: GENM — this is bottom-fishing territory, but the fish is still swimming downward. 🎣😅 📉 Stock Trend 🔴 Weekly: Stage 4 downtrend. Price remains below every major EMA: EMA5 1.582, EMA10 1.710, EMA20 1.838. 🔴 Daily: still lower highs/lower lows and below EMA5/10/20. Price has reached a fresh 52-week low at RM1.46. Weekly lower Bollinger RM1.451 → price is now testing an important extreme zone. 🐟 Bottom-Fishing Signals 🟢 5m RSI 19 / 32 / 40 → heavily oversold short-term. 🟢 MFI 9.4 → extremely washed out. 🟡 Daily MACD histogram has turned slightly positive, suggesting downward momentum is slowing. 🔴 But weekly MACD remains firmly bearish. Therefore: oversold ≠ bottom confirmed. 💰 Operator / Money Flow Not convincing yet. 🔴 Net outflow −RM338K 🔴 XL: about −RM113K 🟢 Large: only slightly positive 🔴 Medium and small money negative. Worse, the money-flow chart deteriorated sharply late in the session while price hit RM1.46. That looks more like late selling pressure than obvious operator accumulation. 🧱 Bid / Ask This is the interesting part 👀 🟢 Bid strength 93% vs 7% ask RM1.46: 1.02M bid RM1.45: 828K bid Very large support wall right at the low. But a huge bid wall is useful only if sellers cannot eat through it. If RM1.46 disappears despite that 1M bid, that becomes a bearish signal rather than bullish. 🎯 Key Levels & Trading Plan 🟢 Potential bottom zone: RM1.45–1.46 🟡 First recovery trigger: RM1.48–1.49 🟢 Better reversal confirmation: RM1.50–1.52 🚀 Stronger trend improvement only above RM1.58 🛑 Below RM1.45 → bottom-fishing thesis weakens materially. 🎯 TP1: RM1.52–1.55 🎯 TP2: RM1.58–1.62 if reversal develops. Aggressive bottom fishing should ideally wait for RM1.45–1.46 to survive another selling attack + bullish candle + improving money flow. Safer traders wait for RM1.49/1.50 reclaim rather than trying to guess the exact bottom. 🧠 Final View Trend 🔴 | Bottom-Fishing Setup 🟡 | Entry Quality 🟡 | Money Flow 🔴 | Oversold 🟢🟢 | Trap Risk 🔴 GENM is very oversold, but not yet a confirmed reversal. The 93% bid strength makes RM1.45–1.46 worth watching closely, but the weekly downtrend and late-session outflow argue against rushing in. The key tomorrow isn't whether GENM looks cheap. It's whether that monster RM1.45–1.46 bid wall actually survives. 🧱👀 Educational analysis only—not financial advice.

title: Malaysia Morning Wrap | Tech Pullback Weighs on Wall Street; KLCI Rises on Blue Chips
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
📌 Key Takeaways
• US stocks end mixed as tech weakens and oil climbs 1.5%
• Nasdaq falls 0.4% at close; Dow gains 0.4%
• KLCI rises 0.59% at close, led by MISC up 6.19%
• Malaysia studies 2027 power subsidies; palm oil inventory jumps 24.5%
• Stocks to Watch: IJM, GENTING, etc.
🇺🇸 Wall Street Summary
$标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ 7,807.24(-0.06%)
$道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ 51,850.55(+0.38%)
$纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ 27,245.90(-0.44%)
U.S. stocks ended mixed on Monday as a pullback in technology shares and firmer oil prices weighed on sentiment. The $纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ fell 120.27 points, or 0.4%, to 27,245.90, while the $标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ slipped 4.30 points, or 0.1%, to 7,807.24. In contrast, the $道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ added 195.60 points, or 0.4%, to 51,850.55. Higher energy prices also added pressure after a Houthi attack on a Saudi civilian airport and after Ukraine said Russia had broken a weekend energy-infrastructure deal. $WTI原油期货主连 (2611) (CLmain.US)$ rose 1.5% to $93.25 a barrel.
Technology names led the downside. $Cerebras Systems (CBRS.US)$ dropped 10.7%, $Lumentum (LITE.US)$ lost 9.8%, and $IonQ Inc (IONQ.US)$ fell 9.1%. Optical peers $Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI.US)$ and $Coherent (COHR.US)$ declined 8.2% and 7.9%, respectively. Memory and AI-linked stocks also retreated, with $美光科技 (MU.US)$ down 3.9%, $英特尔 (INTC.US)$ off 3.2%, $美国超微公司 (AMD.US)$ down 2.3%, $英伟达 (NVDA.US)$ losing 1.3%, and $特斯拉 (TSLA.US)$ shedding 1.2%.
Among gainers, $Meta Platforms (META.US)$ rallied 3.4% after unveiling its Muse Wonder AI agent. Other advances included $赛富时 (CRM.US)$, up 2.1%, $苹果 (AAPL.US)$, up 1.3%, and $耐克 (NKE.US)$, up 1.8%.
🇲🇾 Bursa Market Insight
$富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ 1618.010(+0.59%)
Top Gainer: $MISC (3816.MY)$ RM8.060 (+6.19%)
Top Loser: $MRDIY (5296.MY)$ RM1.190 (-4.80%)
USD/MYR: $美元/马来西亚令吉 (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.0850(-0.02%)
The $富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ rose 9.53 points, or 0.59%, to 1,618.01, supported by gains in selected blue chips. Top gainer $MISC (3816.MY)$ added 6.19% to RM8.06, while top loser $MRDIY (5296.MY)$ fell 4.80% to RM1.19. The ringgit was little changed, with $美元/马来西亚令吉 (USDMYR.FX)$ at 4.0850, down 0.02%.
Malaysia's government is in discussions with Tenaga Nasional and the energy regulator on electricity subsidy measures for 2027, keeping focus on utility pricing, fiscal outlays and inflation transmission. Separately, UOB said gross government borrowings could ease to MYR180 billion in 2027, while CIMB noted the absence of external debt maturities next year may provide more flexibility in funding plans.
In commodities, Malaysia's September palm oil inventory rose 24.5% month on month as production increased and exports declined, a key data point for the plantation sector. Analysts also said a minimum wage hike could lift labour costs for plantation companies, while oil prices fell on expectations a Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire could increase supply.
🔍 IPO Scanner
🔔 Stocks to Watch
$IJM (3336.MY)$ secured a RM1.23 billion contract to build AT&S semiconductor manufacturing facilities in Kulim, Kedah. The job covers construction works for the Austrian group's plant, adding to IJM's order book and marking a major project in Malaysia's semiconductor supply chain.
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ and $GENM (4715.MY)$ remained in focus after the group announced a cash call of more than RM1 billion, while Bursa Malaysia suspended intraday short selling for Genting Malaysia shares and separately halted intraday short selling in Genting after the counter hit the exchange's trigger level. The developments were regulatory and funding-related measures tied to recent trading conditions.
$MNHLDG (0245.MY)$ won a RM294 million contract to develop power infrastructure facilities for a data centre. The contract adds a sizeable data centre-linked job to the group's pipeline and underscores continued project flow in utility works tied to digital infrastructure.
$IOIPG (5249.MY)$ is looking to acquire a 50% stake in One Raffles Place in Singapore. The proposed transaction would give the group exposure to a prime commercial asset in Singapore's central business district, subject to the finalisation of deal terms and approvals.
$MASTEEL (5098.MY)$ plans to acquire a 51% stake in a power infrastructure company for RM12 million. The proposed acquisition would expand the steelmaker's presence into power infrastructure-related activities as part of its business diversification efforts.
$SWIFT (5303.MY)$, via Swift Energy Technology, secured RM59.1 million in orders involving data centres and gas projects. The newly secured jobs strengthen near-term order visibility across engineering works tied to energy and industrial infrastructure.
$INFOM (0265.MY)$ renewed a RM22.1 million contract with Panasonic Digital. The renewal extends the Malaysian technology firm's service engagement with the Japanese client and supports recurring revenue from its software and IT services business.

body: https://youtu.be/7Mx1GOyFU2w?si=176ArZkZCUx50CYR Analysts vs. Rating Agencies: The Truth Behind Genting’s Rights Issue @YZFinanceMY Genting Berhad at a Strategic Crossroads: Balancing Equity Concerns and Balance Sheet Stability Genting Berhad’s proposed RM1.25 billion rights issue highlights the delicate balance between maintaining shareholder equity and protecting credit ratings. The market’s reaction reflects two starkly contrasting perspectives: 1️⃣ Equity Analysts: Expressing concern over potential share dilution and negative market signaling. 2️⃣ Credit Rating Agencies: Supporting the initiative as a necessary step toward debt reduction and balance sheet stabilization. The Financial Pressures Driving the Decision: • Leveraged Share Acquisition: In late 2025, Genting expanded its stake in Genting Malaysia to nearly 74% via a RM3.3 billion purchase, funded primarily through short-term borrowings. • Dividend Constraints: Cash distribution from Genting Malaysia diminished as capital was diverted toward Resorts World New York City’s expansion. • Maturity Wall: As of mid-2026, Genting faces RM9.7 billion in short-term debt obligations, with narrowed long-term refinancing options following credit downgrades. • Capital Drag: Projects like Kasuri LNG continue to consume capital without generating cash flow, while Resorts World Las Vegas remains loss-making due to high financing costs despite strong EBITDA. The Strategic Imperative: Capital Recycling A broader governance issue lies in Genting's attachment to non-performing "strategic assets" (e.g., idle Miami land, PUC shares, and the Bintan casino project via Landmarks). While core operations (Resorts World Genting, Resorts World Sentosa, and Resorts World New York City) remain solid profit drivers, underperforming overseas properties continue to drain capital. To rebuild long-term balance sheet strength, analysts argue that Genting must transition toward disciplined capital recycling—divesting non-core holdings and monetizing idle assets. How can conglomerate boards better execute capital recycling during debt squeezes? Share your thoughts in the comments below. https://youtu.be/7Mx1GOyFU2w?si=176ArZkZCUx50CYR #CorporateStrategy #FinancialRestructuring #Genting #CapitalMarkets #BalanceSheetManagement #Leadership Genting Group at a Strategic Crossroads: Weighing Equity Dilution Against Balance Sheet Stability The MYR 1.25 billion rights issue proposed by Genting Berhad highlights the dilemma companies face in balancing shareholder value preservation with maintaining credit ratings. Capital markets have reacted with two sharply divergent viewpoints: 1️⃣ Equity Analysts: Concerned about equity dilution and the negative signal sent to the market. 2️⃣ Credit Rating Agencies: Express support, viewing it as a viable move to reduce debt and stabilize the balance sheet. Key Financial Drivers Behind the Move: • Leveraged Stake Increase: By the end of 2025, Genting relied primarily on short-term borrowing to raise MYR 3.3 billion, boosting its stake in Genting Malaysia to nearly 74%. • Constrained Dividend Repatriation: Genting Malaysia has reduced dividend payouts to its parent company as capital is being directed toward the expansion of Resorts World New York City. • Mounting Short-Term Debt Pressure: By mid-2026, Genting faces MYR 9.7 billion in maturing short-term debt, while long-term refinancing channels have narrowed following a credit rating downgrade. • Capital-draining items: The Kasuri LNG project continues to consume capital without generating cash flow, while Resorts World Las Vegas, despite strong EBITDA, remains loss-making due to high financing costs. Strategic transformation is imminent: Rebalancing the asset portfolio Beyond debt pressure, Genting’s long-term retention of “strategic assets” (such as idle land in Miami, PUC shares, and Landmarks equity held for the Bintan Island casino project) has become a burden during periods of tight liquidity. While Resorts World Genting, Resorts World Singapore, and Resorts World New York continue to serve as strong profit engines, projects in Las Vegas, the Catskills, Bimini, and Birmingham have failed to deliver commensurate investment returns. Analysts point out that if Genting is to revitalize its balance sheet and restore market confidence, it must adopt a rigorous “capital recovery” strategy—monetizing idle assets, divesting non-core businesses, and concentrating resources on high-return, quality projects. How do you view Genting’s future strategic layout? What are Warrants?
Structured warrants are leveraged financial instruments issued by a third party, which are namely banks and financial institutions. Structured warrants derive their value from, and generally move in greater percentages than, the price movements in the underlying assets that they track.
Types of Warrants
1. A call warrant gives investors the theoretical right, but not the obligation, to buy the underlying asset for a particular price. In case of a ‘cash-settled’ call warrant, the investor will receive a cash payment based on such price. Typically, the price of a call warrant increases as the underlying asset price goes up, and decreases when the underlying asset price goes down.
1. A put warrant gives investors the theoretical right, but not the obligation, to sell an underlying asset for a particular price. In case of a ‘cash-settled’ put warrant, the investor will receive a cash payment based on such price. Typically, the price of a put warrant increases as the underlying asset price goes down, and decreases when the underlying asset price goes up.
Why trade Warrants?
•⁠ Provide leverage
•⁠ Limited loss
•⁠ Lower capital outlay
•⁠ Gain exposure, whether bullish or bearish, with calls and puts available
•⁠ Traded on an exchange, with market makers providing liquidity
For detailed explanations on various warrant topics, you can click into the Warrant Education section on Macquarie's warrants website. In addition to their Moo Community page, you may also subscribe to Macquarie's newsletter and follow them on Telegram and Facebook to receive up-to-date news and information about warrants.
Macquarie Warrants Malaysia provides transparent pricing with the Live Matrix, which is directly connected to its market-making system, and indicates where their bid and offer prices would be in a warrant, based on various price points in the stock or index.

title: Foreign Funds Dump Utilities as Retail Investors Step In on Bursa Malaysia
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Energy prices are back in the driver’s seat—and markets are feeling every bump. The latest MBSB Fund Flow Report shows inflation worries rising, global equities moving in different directions, and foreign investors staying cautious across much of Asia. In Malaysia, meanwhile, retail investors kept buying even as foreign and local institutions turned sellers.
Market Pulse：Global Economy at a Glance
Energy was the week’s big spoiler. US September headline CPI rose 3.7% year-on-year, while core inflation reached 2.6%. Producer prices were even hotter: headline PPI jumped 1.3% month-on-month and 6.3% year-on-year.
Consumers, however, were still spending. US retail sales rose 0.8% month-on-month, beating expectations, helped by higher gasoline spending. Markets reacted unevenly: FTSE 100 gained 3.1%, Sensex added 3.1%, and DAX 40 rose 2.1%, while the S&P 500 fell 2.0%, Nasdaq lost 4.5%, and Nikkei dropped 5.4%.
Brent crude climbed 4.9% to US$109.86 per barrel. The ringgit strengthened 0.1% against the US dollar to RM4.0810. Bottom line? Inflation fears are back, but risk appetite has not disappeared.
Asia’s Money Moves：Foreign Investors Stay Defensive
Across the eight Asian markets monitored, foreign investors extended their selling streak to three weeks, pulling out a combined US$28.32bn. Most markets recorded outflows, while Thailand was the sole market to attract foreign money, with net inflows of US$113.9m.
South Korea saw US$8.33bn in net outflows, its ninth consecutive week of selling, despite strong export-price and export-value growth. India recorded US$830.4m in outflows as inflation accelerated to 5.54%, driven by higher food, transport and restaurant prices.
Indonesia lost US$176.5m after MSCI proposed removing the country from its Emerging Markets Index, raising concerns over transparency and trading practices. Vietnam saw US$116.2m leave the market, even as trade negotiations with the US moved closer to completion.
Malaysia Breakdown：Retail Buys While Institutions Sell
Bursa Malaysia remained under foreign pressure in the week ended 16 October. Foreign institutions sold RM270.2m net, extending their selling streak to four consecutive weeks. They were net sellers on all five trading days, with Monday recording the largest outflow of RM105.7m, followed by Wednesday’s RM84.6m.
Local institutions also turned sellers, recording RM140.3m in net outflows after three straight weeks of net buying. Retail investors moved in the opposite direction. They extended their buying streak to eight weeks, accumulating RM410.5m net.
Trading activity was mixed. Retail average daily trading volume fell 13.4%, while local-institution and foreign-institution participation rose by 4.4% and 4.8%, respectively.
Foreign buying was focused on Financial Services, which attracted RM88.5m, followed by Healthcare at RM55.5m and Transportation & Logistics at RM52.8m. On the selling side, Utilities saw RM201.3m in outflows, followed by Industrial Products & Services at RM131.3m and Plantation at RM75.8m.
Stock Spotlight: Who’s Buying What?
Local Retail's Top Buys:
$PMETAL (8869.MY)$ （RM63.9m)
$MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ (RM53.9m)
$GENM (4715.MY)$ (RM39.1m)
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ (RM33.1m)
Local Institutions' Top Buys:
$TENAGA (5347.MY)$ (RM176.1m)
$MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ (RM122.5m)
$SUNWAY (5211.MY)$ (RM32.9m)
$IOICORP (1961.MY)$ (RM24.2m)
Foreign Investors' Top Sells:
$TENAGA (5347.MY)$ (RM-173.0m)
$MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ (RM-169.4m)
$PMETAL (8869.MY)$ (RM-50.7m)
$SUNWAY (5211.MY)$ (RM-29.8m)
Strategy Breakdown: Who Is Playing What?
Local Institutions: Rotation Rather Than a Full Exit?
Local institutions were net sellers overall, but their buying of Tenaga Nasional, Malayan Banking and Sunway Construction points to selective positioning rather than a broad market retreat.
The pattern looks mixed. They added exposure to utilities, banks and construction, but reduced holdings in CIMB, Public Bank, Press Metal and UWC. This may reflect stock-specific rotation, though the report does not provide enough information to determine long-term holding intentions.
Local Retail: Buying Into Familiar Names
Retail investors continued to buy aggressively, favouring Press Metal, Malayan Banking, Genting-linked counters and YTL Power. This suggests continued interest in liquid, familiar names and active themes such as aluminium, banking and utilities.
At the same time, retail investors sold Top Glove and Public Bank. The behaviour shows a more tactical approach: investors were not simply buying the market, but rotating between individual stocks.
Foreign Investors: Banks In, Utilities Out
Foreign institutions were net sellers overall, yet they selectively accumulated Public Bank, CIMB and Top Glove. Their biggest exits were Tenaga Nasional and Malayan Banking.
This is a notable split. Foreign funds appeared willing to add selected financial names while reducing exposure to utilities, industrials and plantation stocks at the sector level. The report does not provide evidence of currency hedging or a specific global-allocation strategy, but the overall outflow trend signals continued caution.
Why Are the Three Groups So Different?
The gap may come down to investor type. Retail investors can react faster to stock stories and short-term price movements. Local institutions may rotate between large-cap names while balancing portfolio requirements. Foreign investors, meanwhile, remain influenced by wider regional fund flows, global inflation concerns and risk sentiment.
Risks to Watch
The biggest near-term risk is still inflation. Higher US energy costs pushed both consumer and producer prices higher, while Brent crude moved above US$109 per barrel. If energy prices stay elevated, pressure on global interest-rate expectations and equity valuations could increase.
Regional fund flows are another concern. Foreign investors continued to pull money from Asian equities, while Indonesia’s proposed MSCI index removal added to market uncertainty. For Malaysia, continued foreign selling—especially in utilities, industrials and plantation stocks—could keep trading conditions volatile.
For now, Bursa Malaysia is seeing an interesting tug-of-war: foreign funds are stepping back, but local retail investors are still willing to buy.

title: We are completely helpless against the Genting group's downward trend.
author: 风起云涌LBF
body:
It feels like a company on the verge of collapse, with its stock price sliding continuously and shareholders constantly selling off... But looking back 10 years ago, the YTL group was in the same situation~ with no buying support whatsoever~ yet in reality, the YTL founding family emerged unscathed.

The Genting group is puzzling~ I'm confused too.. No more buying~ Sell on any rebound to recover some capital~ Right now, cash is more needed than stocks (but the prerequisite is that your average holding cost for GENTING should be around 2.3-2.5, and for GENM around 1.8)~ This way, if it drops further, you can enter at a 1:2 ratio~ Then arbitrage and exit when it rebounds close to your average holding cost.

Reduce losses~ Seize opportunities to execute more buy-low, sell-high strategies.

title: Foreign Funds Dump Malaysia, Yet Banks Still Get Gobbled Up
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Global uncertainty set the tone for the week ended 23 October 2026. Foreign money continued to leave Asian equities, including Malaysia, but the selling was far from uniform. On Bursa Malaysia, foreign investors sold plantations, industrial names and utilities, while still buying selected banks. So, is this a broad exit—or a selective reshuffle? Let’s break it down.
Market Pulse: Global Economy,Resilient US, Nervous Markets
US data remained firm: the Manufacturing PMI rose to 56.0 in October, while initial jobless claims fell to 194,000, their lowest since mid-July. But housing starts dropped 5.2% month-on-month in September as high mortgage rates hurt demand. Elsewhere, Eurozone business activity slowed, with the Composite PMI easing to 51.9. Rising inflation also remained a concern in Japan and China.
Risk appetite was weak overall. Only five of 20 major indices tracked ended higher. Brent crude jumped 6.2% to USD116.72 a barrel, while the US dollar gained 0.1% against the ringgit to RM4.0857. The FBM KLCI still edged up 0.24%, but global uncertainty kept investors cautious.
Asia’s Money Moves: Foreign Money Stays on the Sidelines
Foreign investors extended their selling streak across the eight Asian markets monitored, with total weekly net outflows reaching USD8.75 billion. India was the biggest recipient of foreign buying, attracting USD426.1 million, while Thailand recorded USD89.3 million in net inflows.
Selling pressure was also visible in South Korea, Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia and Vietnam. South Korea saw USD1.05 billion leave the market, while Indonesia lost USD369.6 million. The Philippines recorded USD144.1 million of outflows and Vietnam saw USD37.4 million leave.
The backdrop was mixed: resilient economic activity in India contrasted with rate decisions, inflation pressures, elevated oil prices and policy uncertainty across the region. In short, investors were not abandoning Asia entirely—but they were clearly becoming more selective.
Malaysia Breakdown: Foreign Selling Hits Five-Week Mark
Foreign institutions extended their net-selling streak on Bursa Malaysia to five consecutive weeks, recording net outflows of RM301.7 million for the week ended 23 October. They sold on three of the five trading days, with the largest outflow on Tuesday at RM187.0 million. Friday and Thursday also saw net selling of RM118.0 million and RM97.6 million respectively.
Still, foreign activity was selective. Financial Services attracted RM261.6 million in foreign inflows, followed by Healthcare at RM38.9 million and Property at RM9.2 million. On the other side, Plantation saw RM172.3 million of outflows, while Industrial Products & Services and Utilities lost RM150.0 million and RM147.6 million respectively.
Local institutions returned to net buying, adding RM205.0 million after selling in the previous week. Retail investors also stayed positive, extending their buying streak to nine weeks with RM96.8 million in net purchases.
Trading activity cooled across the board. Average daily trading volume fell 23.2% for foreign institutions, 15.3% for local institutions and 21.5% for retailers. That suggests investors were trading more cautiously, even as local money absorbed part of the foreign selling.
Stock Spotlight: Who’s Buying What?
Local Retail's Top Buys:
$MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ (RM67.5m)
$CIMB (1023.MY)$ (RM50.6m)
$GENM (4715.MY)$ (RM17.1m）
$IOICORP (1961.MY)$ （RM14.2m）
Local Institutions' Top Buys:
$SDG (5285.MY)$ (RM143.8m)
$PMETAL (8869.MY)$ (RM125.1m)
$TENAGA (5347.MY)$ (RM115.4m)
$MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ (RM39.5m)
Foreign Investors' Top Sells:
$SDG (5285.MY)$ (RM-142.1m)
$PMETAL (8869.MY)$ (RM-110.7m)
$MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ (RM-104.1m)
$TENAGA (5347.MY)$ (RM-101.0m)
Strategy Breakdown: Three Investor Groups, Three Different Playbooks
Local institutions appeared to favour large, liquid names such as SD Guthrie, Press Metal and Tenaga Nasional. Their buying was concentrated in plantation, industrial and utility-linked companies, while they reduced exposure to several banks. This points to a selective rotation rather than a blanket move into or out of equities.
Retail investors leaned heavily into Malayan Banking and CIMB, while also picking up Genting Malaysia, IOI Properties and Inari Amertron. At the same time, they sold Top Glove and Gamuda. Their flows show a mix of interest in familiar large-cap names, property and technology.
Foreign investors were net sellers overall, but they were not selling every bank. Public Bank, CIMB and AMMB attracted foreign inflows, even as Malayan Banking saw significant outflows. Foreign selling was heavier in plantation, industrial products, utilities and selected construction names.
Why the difference? Fund flows alone do not reveal every investor’s motivation. Still, the gap may reflect different investment horizons, liquidity needs, risk appetite and portfolio positioning. The clearest message is this: broad foreign selling did not stop stock-specific buying.
Risks to Watch: What Could Shake Sentiment Next?
Global uncertainty remains the key risk. Higher energy prices, policy uncertainty and uneven economic data could keep market volatility elevated. Rising Brent crude may also feed into inflation concerns, while high borrowing costs continue to pressure housing activity in the US.
For Malaysia, persistent foreign outflows remain worth watching, especially if they broaden beyond the sectors already under pressure. Lower trading participation also signals caution. Investors may want to focus not only on headline fund flows, but also on where money is still entering the market—because that is where the real story is.

🎢 GENM (4715) — The Rebound Has Arrived, but Has the Downtrend Really Ended?
📅 28 October 2026 | 11:18 AM | RM1.220 (+6.09%)
📈 STOCK TREND
– 🔴 Weekly: Stage 4 downtrend remains intact. Price is still below all major EMAs.
– 🟢 Daily: Strong rebound from RM1.090, now reclaiming EMA8 (RM1.196).
– 🟡 Daily EMA20 (RM1.281) remains the next major technical hurdle.
– 🟢 5-min: Bullish intraday structure, but price is consolidating near RM1.220.
– Setup: Early reversal attempt within a larger bearish trend — not yet a confirmed Stage 2 recovery.
📊 BOTTOM-FISHING & MOMENTUM
– 🟢 Weekly RSI 25.46 — Deeply oversold, supporting rebound potential.
– 🔴 Weekly MACD -0.096 — Longer-term selling momentum remains negative.
– 🟢 Daily RSI 51.09 — Improving momentum and recovering above neutral.
– 🟡 Daily MFI 38.20 — Buying pressure recovering, but still relatively weak.
– ⚠️ 5-min MFI 16.60 — Short-term buying momentum has cooled sharply despite elevated prices.
– ⚠️ 5-min MACD histogram -0.003 — Possible short-term consolidation or pullback.
– The rebound has technical merit, but intraday momentum is no longer accelerating.
💰 MONEY FLOW & OPERATOR OVERSIGHT
– 🟢 Net inflow: RM2.265M.
– 🟢 XL: +RM789K.
– 🟢 Large: +RM522K.
– 🟢 Medium: +RM748K.
– 🟢 Small: +RM206K.
– ✅ Positive inflow across all trade sizes, particularly XL and large transactions.
– 🟢 Daily volume already 6.17M shares, exceeding the previous session's approximately 4.71M.
– Interpretation: Meaningful buying participation supports the rebound, although it does not establish confirmed institutional accumulation.
– Possible demand zone: RM1.150–1.200, based on the recent rebound structure, not a verified operator cost.
🧱 BID/ASK PRESSURE
– 🔴 Bid 27.70% versus ask 72.30%.
– RM1.200: 598K displayed bid.
– RM1.190: 700K displayed bid.
– RM1.220: 296K displayed ask.
– RM1.230: 399K displayed ask.
– RM1.250: 480K displayed ask.
– ⚠️ Overhead supply is building between RM1.220–1.250.
– Buyers need to absorb these offers rather than merely maintain the current price.
⚠️ TRAP RISK
– Weekly oversold conditions can produce sharp rallies without ending the downtrend.
– The RM1.220–1.250 zone could become a short-term profit-taking area.
– The divergence between strong cumulative inflow and falling 5-min MFI deserves attention.
– A rejection followed by a break below RM1.190 would weaken the rebound thesis.
🎯 KEY LEVELS
– Immediate support: RM1.200 / RM1.190.
– Stronger support: RM1.150–1.170.
– Critical invalidation: RM1.090.
– Immediate resistance: RM1.220–1.250.
– Major resistance: RM1.280–1.300.
– Higher recovery target: RM1.350–1.380.
📋 TRADING PLAN
– 🟡 Aggressive entry: RM1.180–1.200 on a controlled, low-volume pullback that holds support.
– 🟢 Safer entry: Confirmed breakout above RM1.250 with increased volume, preferably followed by a successful retest.
– 🛑 Aggressive cut-loss: Below RM1.150.
– 🛑 Breakout-entry cut-loss: Below RM1.200 if the retest fails.
– 🎯 TP1: RM1.250.
– 🎯 TP2: RM1.280–1.300.
– Extended target: RM1.350 if the daily trend improves.
– Existing holders: RM1.220–1.250 is an important area to monitor for selling pressure; a partial profit-taking strategy may be considered.
– Fresh buyers: Avoid chasing RM1.220 directly into resistance without a favourable risk/reward setup.
– Setup cancellation: Sustained loss of RM1.150 or renewed heavy selling that erases the rebound.
⭐ BUYING RATING: 5.5/10 — SPECULATIVE REBOUND
– Trend confidence: 8/10 bearish higher-timeframe bias.
– Setup confidence: 6/10.
– Current entry quality: 4/10.
– Grade: B- for a countertrend rebound; not yet an A-grade reversal.
🚦 FINAL VIEW
– ✅ Strong positive XL/L/M inflow suggests the rebound has genuine buying participation.
– ✅ Improving daily RSI and reclaiming EMA8 are constructive.
– ⚠️ Weak weekly trend and overhead selling supply remain substantial.
– Above RM1.250: Rebound continuation becomes more convincing.
– Above RM1.280–1.300: Early evidence of a more sustainable trend recovery.
– Below RM1.190: Risk of renewed selling increases.
Verdict: GENM is showing an encouraging bottom-fishing rebound with meaningful buying flow. However, the higher-timeframe bearish structure remains intact. A successful retest near RM1.190–1.200 offers a more disciplined setup than chasing into RM1.220–1.250 resistance. 🐂
❓ Is the positive XL inflow the beginning of sustained accumulation, or will sellers reappear around RM1.250?
Educational analysis only — not financial advice.
